units.question: My Thai tourist extension runs out one day before my flight home. What actually happens at the airport if I leave a single day late?
units.gold: A one-day overstay in Thailand is treated leniently. The usual penalty is a 500 baht fine per day, but one traveller who left from Don Mueang a day late was told by immigration officers that a single day did not even require the fine, and that two or more days would. Instead of a large OVERSTAY stamp, you may get only a small Thai annotation near the departure stamp. The same traveller later obtained a student visa without problems.
rubric: States the overstay fine is 500 baht per day
Notes that a single day overstay may be waived, with fines applying from two days
Mentions only a small Thai note/stamp rather than a big OVERSTAY stamp
Says a later visa was still granted without trouble
Penalize: claiming a one-day overstay leads to a ban or blacklisting
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
If you leave a single day late, you may be denied entry or require a new visa application, depending on the airport's policies and the country's immigration rules.

[3] Mount Marapi
Mythology: According to legend, the mountain is where the Minangkabau people first settled after their ship landed on the mountain when it was the size of an egg and surrounded by water. There are large numbers of burial stones in the region which are facing in the direction of the mountain, showing that it is important to their culture.

[4] Mount Marapi
Eruptions: The volcano has a known history of eruptions. Marapi had a large eruption in September 1830. In January 1975 an eruption occurred with mudflows and lahars that caused fatalities in the surrounding area. A large eruption happened in 1979, which killed 60 people. At least one person was killed during an eruption in 1996. In April–May 2018 ashfalls to the southeast occurred.

Since 2011, the volcano has been at the second level of a four-tier alert system made by the Volcanological Survey of Indonesia. Predicting the volcano's behavior is hard because the source of its eruptions are shallow and near its peak, while its eruptions are not caused by a deep movement of magma that can be detected as volcanic earthquakes on seismic monitors. Even though there are common eruptions, there are about 1,400 people living on the mountain's slopes in the villages of Rubai and Gobah Cumantiang, which are about 5 to 6 kilometers from the summit.

[5] What would happen if you miss the bag drop-off deadline and it's kind of the airline's fault for bad ground service?
Tags: air-travel, luggage

I turned up at the airport today in what I would consider moderate but not great (since the train was late) time:

- 35 minutes before bag drop-off closed.
- 75 minutes before departure.

To cut a long story short, there was an incredibly long line and only 3 counters open. I was able to squeeze in the priority line and had 3 minutes to spare before the 'bag drop-off deadline'.

There were people behind me who would have been past the deadline. I'm curious what would have happened to them?

- I've heard about boarding being denied for turning up 1 minute late.
- Then again, it's partially the ground staff's fault for being inadequately staffed.

What would have been the likely fate of these passengers?

units.question: Does a one-year Hungarian residence card let an Indian citizen fly home and return, even though the visa sticker in the passport says single entry?
units.gold: Yes. The single-entry visa is used up once you have entered the Schengen area, so it cannot be reused. But it is not needed: under Article 5 of the Schengen Borders Code, third-country nationals need a visa except where they hold a valid residence permit or long-stay visa. As long as the Hungarian residence permit is still valid, it alone allows re-entry, even with a new passport that does not contain the old visa.
rubric: Says the single-entry visa cannot be reused after its one entry
Says a valid residence permit is enough to re-enter without a visa
Cites the Schengen Borders Code (Article 5) exception for residence permit holders
Notes the permit must still be valid on return
Penalize: telling the person they must apply for a new visa to come back
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
A one-year Hungarian residence card does not affect the visa entry requirements. The visa sticker indicating single entry is separate from the residence card. You can return to India with the residence card and the same visa.
units.sources:
[1] What happens if there is no space for entry stamp in the passport for US visa?
Tags: usa, customs-and-immigration, passports, indian-citizens, passport-stamps I hold an Indian passport and have an F-1 Visa (multiple entry) for USA. I applied for a Schengen visa and it got approved but the Italian consulate has affixed the schengen visa sticker in a page which comes before my US Visa. For example, my US Visa sticker is in page 20 while my Schengen Visa is now in page 15.

[2] The barcode sticker which VFS in India puts on the back of my passport got damaged by water. Will this cause me problems upon re-entering India?
Answers > Answer (score 21): The VFS affixed a barcode sticker to the back of your passport; this is so that they can track when your passport is sent to the consulate, received at the consulate, returned to the VFS, and returned to the applicant. Each time the sticker is scanned a computer system is updated with the new status.

The sticker is meaningless to the end-user and it is irrelevant once your passport has been returned to you.

Is this a serious issue and would I be barred from entering India when I fly back?

No, the sticker can be removed once you take possession of your passport. It's not a big deal at all.

[3] Can I go back to my native country and come back again with a residence permit and a single entry visa?
Tags: visas, customs-and-immigration, indian-citizens, hungary

I am an Indian and now in Hungary, the visa stamped in my passport is marked as single entry but I have a residence permit valid for 1 year. Can I go back to India and come again with the same visa?

units.question: I'm helping my father with his US DS-160 and he has had dozens of school jobs over 25 years. Does he need to enter every one?
units.gold: No. The DS-160 FAQ asks only for the applicant's previous two employers. Applicants who want to be thorough may bring a separate written list of all previous employers to the visa interview for reference. Forgetting a short job from decades ago is not normally a reason for refusal; US officials care mainly about links to criminal or terrorist organisations.
rubric: States the DS-160 asks for only the previous two employers
Mentions the option of bringing a full written list of employers to the interview
Reassures that omitting old minor jobs is not normally grounds for refusal
Penalize: claiming every job from the past 25 years must be listed
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
The DS-160 form requires entering information about your previous two employers only, so you don't need to list all of your school jobs. You should focus on the most relevant ones and avoid including details you don't remember.

Tags: visas, usa My dad and I are filling out the DS-160 Visa form online. We got to where he is asked to list all of his previous employment. The problem is that he has worked in a lot of schools in the past 25 years.

[2] How can I support myself financially as a 17 year old with a loan?
Tags: united-states, loans, financial-literacy, car I'm a 17 year old Ohio high school student who makes ~$160 a month working minimum wage. Monthly payments are ~$80 for the car plus an additional $70 for part of insurance (my father helps pay since I'm required to have full coverage). I'm struggling to maintain a steady and reliable flow of income with this job and haven't been able to find another after ~3 months of applying to dozens of jobs with only three follow-ups and no interviews.

[3] Do I have to list all of the previous employment information in the DS-160 visa form?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): No. The DS-160 FAQ says enter information regarding your previous two employers only.

[4] Do I have to list all of the previous employment information in the DS-160 visa form?
Answers > Answer (score 3): He should list as many as he remembers. Do not fret over those he does not remember. The USA is primarily concerned with working for or affiliation with terror sponsoring organizations, criminal enterprises, and terrorist organizations. He will not be refused because he worked for some school twenty years ago for a few months and forgot to include it.

How do I know? Because during my green card and citizenship process I forgot some minor companies I briefly worked for and it was not a problem. Note that green card and citizenship applications are scrutinized even more stringently than visa applications.

[5] DS-160 Present work/ education/ training information
Tags: f1-visas

I completed my master's last year from India and have not been involved with any other institution since. I have been accepted to a US university for pursuing Ph.D. and am in the process of filling the DS-160. I understand that I am required to fill my current position as "Not employed", could you kindly let me know if that would affect my chances of getting a F-1 VISA? Also the DS-160 requires an explanation for not employed. Over the past couple of months I have prepared for and written the GRE, qualified entrance exams for PhD in India and was able to publish a paper in a peer reviewed international journal. Should I mention this in the explanation? If not, what am I supposed to write?

[6] DS-160 - I was asked more questions than my mom, is that normal?
Answers > Answer (score 4, accepted): It appears that this section is required of only some applicants, depending on their occupation or nationality:

Please note that this page will be displayed if the Additional Work/Education/Training page is not required (this page is required for nationals of certain countries as discussed below).

And

Present and Past Work/Education/Training Information

This page is displayed for all applicants with varying amount of information required depending on the Primary Occupation chosen.

units.question: List what an American visiting France for about three weeks should carry at the border besides the passport.
units.gold: No visa is needed, but formally she must meet the same entry conditions as visa travellers: a valid purpose (an invitation helps), enough money for the stay and a way to leave, such as a return or onward ticket. The return ticket is what border guards most often check. France's reference amount for means of subsistence is EUR 65 per day, and a credit card may be enough proof. Travel health insurance is not required for visa-exempt visitors, though it is a good idea.
rubric: Says no visa is required for a US citizen on a short visit
Recommends a return or onward ticket as the most likely thing checked
Mentions sufficient funds, with France's reference of EUR 65 per day (a credit card may suffice)
States travel insurance is not mandatory for visa-exempt visitors
Penalize: saying a US citizen needs a Schengen visa or ESTA for France
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Besides the passport, carry a valid visa, travel insurance, and a photo ID.
units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: France
Get in > By car > From the United Kingdom: The Channel Tunnel provides a rail and road connection between South East England and France. Shuttle trains operated by Eurotunnel carry vehicles from Folkestone in Kent to Calais (Hauts-de-France) in 35 minutes, though you only spend about 20 minutes in the tunnel itself. Passengers remain with their vehicles for the duration, with trips to the toilet allowed. In the reverse direction, you will go through British passport control in France before driving onto the train.

[2] Wikivoyage: France
Get in > Entry requirements: Foreign nationals who are not visa-exempt must make a déclaration d'entrée (declaration of entry) at a police station or to border inspection personnel if they arrive in France directly from another country of the Schengen Area, unless they hold a long-term visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen member state. Their passports will be endorsed by the authorities to prove that such a declaration has been made. If you intend to stay in France for longer than 90 days, regardless of purpose, an advance long-stay visa is always required, except for EEA and Swiss citizens. It is almost impossible to switch from a "C" (visitor) entry status to a "D" (long-stay) status from inside France.

[3] Wikivoyage: France
France is a country with which almost every traveller has a relationship. Many dream of its joie de vivre shown by the countless cafés, picturesque villages, and world-famous gastronomy. Some come to follow the trail of France's great philosophers, writers and artists, or to immerse in the beautiful language it gave to the world. Others still are drawn to the country's geographical diversity, with its long coastlines, massive mountain ranges and breathtaking farmland vistas.

[4] When do dual citizens (Canadian & American citizenship) need to file U.S. income taxes?
Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): The short answer, per the IRS, is yes.

Whether the IRS will come after you, whether you should renounce your US citizenship or what the Republicans will do, I can't answer. If you're really concerned with the question of legality, I'd recommend to talk to an international tax lawyer.

(As an aside, if you do decide to file you can simply request an ITIN number, no need for SSN and passport - follow the link from the above linked article)

[5] When do dual citizens (Canadian & American citizenship) need to file U.S. income taxes?
Answers > Answer (score 4): Renouncing your citizenship would not remove your tax obligation from past years, and may not remove your tax obligation for the future.

In fact, beginning the process of renouncing your citizenship may trigger a review of your tax records.

See Renunciation of U.S. Citizenship from the U.S. Department of State, especially section E. TAX & MILITARY OBLIGATIONS /NO ESCAPE FROM PROSECUTION.

[6] Staying more than 90 days in Schengen area as a French citizen, but only have a US passport
Answers > Answer (score 27, accepted): Regardless of the legality it will be infinitely easier for you to travel if you have a French passport. I suggest contacting your local consulate with whatever documentation you have (birth certificate of your and preferably proof of citizenship of your parents).

You can certainly enter France with a US passport and try to sort it out locally while you are in France. Just make sure you carry all documentation that you may need.

Provided you meet all the criteria to be a French citizen, it's probably not illegal for you to stay for more than 90 days, but if you get checked after 90 days with only your US passport, you will have a LOT of explaining to do. Passport checks at Schengen borders are rare but they do happen occasionally and you will have to show it when you leave Schengen. Hotels may also want to see your passport when you check in.

Recommendation: sort it your before you travel.

units.question: Is there an airside connection between JFK terminals for passengers changing between two domestic flights?
units.gold: Generally no. At JFK the only way between terminals is to leave the secure area and take the AirTrain or a shuttle bus, then clear security again at the new terminal. The exception noted is Delta, which runs Terminals 2 and 4 and has operated a bus linking their airside areas. Allow extra time, because TSA lines at the second terminal can eat much of a connection.
rubric: States there is no general airside link between JFK terminals
Says you must exit, use AirTrain or a shuttle bus, and re-clear security
Mentions the Delta airside bus between Terminals 2 and 4 as an exception
Penalize: claiming JFK has an airside train like DFW's Skylink
units.answer: No airside connections exist between JFK terminals for domestic flights [2]. Passengers must exit the terminal, take the AirTrain or shuttle bus, and re-clear security.
units.sources:
[1] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Is it possible to move between terminals at JFK from within the airside / departures area? Or is the only option when changing between domestic flights at different terminals to exit, take the air-train, then queue up and re-clear security?

[2] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 1): It really depends on the airport. At JFK I recently arrived in Terminal 2 on DL and had to transfer to an AF flight departing Terminal 1. I took the bus from Terminal 4 to Terminal 2, exited the airside and then had to re-clear security at Terminal 1 (a bit of an irritating experience given that there are limited TSA pre-check options at T1). My two hour connection time was whittled down to 30 minutes after the TSA line at T1.

[3] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 9, accepted): No. The only way to get from one terminal to another is to exit the terminal and take the air train or a shuttle bus.

A possible exception to this is for Delta, which operates in Terminals 2 and 4. They apparently have a bus that connects the airside areas of these terminals. See the map here: http://www.delta.com/content/www/en_US/traveling-with-us/airports-and-aircraft/airports/new-york-jfk.html

Indications are that this bus will disappear at some point, presumably when construction of a direct link between the two areas has been completed.

[4] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Tags: usa, transit, airport-security, jfk, airport-terminals

When arriving at JFK (or any US airport) on an international flight that didn't have pre-clearance, I know that you have to clear immigration, collect your bags, clear customs, re-drop bags, change terminals by AirTrain if needed, and then go through security, no matter what terminals are involved.

I also know that when you fly into JFK on a domestic or pre-cleared flight, and your onward flight is from that same terminal, you just step off your domestic flight into the departures area and walk to your onward gate, without needing to do security again.

At some other big US airports I've been to before (eg DFW), there is an airside transfer train that lets you move between terminals, so you can go from gate to gate without needing to exit + re-clear security. However, at JFK the only transfer train I'm aware of is AirTrain, which is landside.

[5] JFK-Arriving Int'l Transfer Passengers required to undergo TSA screening?
An international arrival followed by a transfer does not always imply a terminal change. This question is different from At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? because it is possible to arrive and transfer within the SAME terminal. For example, arrive at JFK T5 on Jetblue from an international flight and transfer within the same terminal to another Jetblue domestic flight. As phoog has pointed out, the question the question is more complicated in that it is comprises international complications, not merely a domestic flight.

When arriving at JFK (or any US airport) on an international flight that didn't have pre-clearance, I know that you have to clear immigration, collect your bags, clear customs, re-drop bags, change terminals by AirTrain if needed, and then go through security, no matter what terminals are involved.

I also know that when you fly into JFK on a domestic or pre-cleared flight, and your onward flight is from that same terminal, you just step off your domestic flight into the departures area and walk to your onward gate, without needing to do security again.

At some other big US airports I've been to before (eg DFW), there is an airside transfer train that lets you move between terminals, so you can go from gate to gate without needing to exit + re-clear security. However, at JFK the only transfer train I'm aware of is AirTrain, which is landside.

[3] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 9, accepted): No. The only way to get from one terminal to another is to exit the terminal and take the air train or a shuttle bus.

A possible exception to this is for Delta, which operates in Terminals 2 and 4. They apparently have a bus that connects the airside areas of these terminals. See the map here: http://www.delta.com/content/www/en_US/traveling-with-us/airports-and-aircraft/airports/new-york-jfk.html

Indications are that this bus will disappear at some point, presumably when construction of a direct link between the two areas has been completed.

[4] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 1): It really depends on the airport. At JFK I recently arrived in Terminal 2 on DL and had to transfer to an AF flight departing Terminal 1. I took the bus from Terminal 4 to Terminal 2, exited the airside and then had to re-clear security at Terminal 1 (a bit of an irritating experience given that there are limited TSA pre-check options at T1). My two hour connection time was whittled down to 30 minutes after the TSA line at T1.

[5] At JFK, can you move between terminals airside on domestic flights? (cited)
Is it possible to move between terminals at JFK from within the airside / departures area? Or is the only option when changing between domestic flights at different terminals to exit, take the air-train, then queue up and re-clear security?

units.question: Give me the easiest public transport route from London Gatwick to Paddington station with luggage.
units.gold: The classic route is the Gatwick Express to Victoria (about 30 minutes, every 15 minutes, station attached to the South Terminal), then the Circle line to Paddington (about 20 minutes). A smoother option with bags is Thameslink to Farringdon, where the rail and Underground lines run side by side, then the Circle or Hammersmith & City line to Paddington in about 14 minutes. You can buy one combined rail-and-tube ticket at the Gatwick ticket office.
rubric: Mentions Gatwick Express to Victoria (around 30 minutes) then the Circle line
Mentions Thameslink to Farringdon as an easier change with luggage
Gives the Farringdon to Paddington leg as about 14 minutes
Notes a combined rail plus tube ticket can be bought at Gatwick
Penalize: routing via Heathrow Express or other wrong airports
units.answer: The easiest route is the Gatwick Express to Victoria Station, then the Tube to Paddington [2]. It takes about 30 minutes and avoids luggage handling.

[1] How to get from Gatwick airport to Paddington? (cited)
Tags: public-transport, airport-transfer, london, lgw What's the most straightforward way to get from Gatwick airport to Paddington station in London using public transport? I'm mostly interested in travel time & general smoothness of the trip (e.g. buying just one ticket for the whole trip would be nice). Price is a secondary concern.

[2] How to get from Gatwick airport to Paddington? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 11, accepted): The most straightforward way would be taking the Gatwick Express to Victoria Station (the journey is about 30 mins). The Gatwick Station is directly connected to the South Terminal. From the North Terminal it's a bit further and you need to take the automated shuttle train. Trains leave every 15 minutes.

From Victoria Station you have no less than three options:

- take the underground/tube/metro/whatever-you-call-it Circle Line (High Street Kensington direction) and get out at Paddington stop. It's gonna take about 20 minutes.
- Accordingly to Gagravarr's comment you could also go from Victoria Line to Oxford Circus, then a cross-platform change to the Bakerloo Line up to Paddington.
- If the metro is closed, take the bus 436 to Paddington.

For all those options, make sure you use the exit at the front of the train, not the exit on the upper floor through the elevators or escalators.

You could also take a taxi, if the price isn't a concern for you.

[3] How to get from Gatwick airport to Paddington? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 11, accepted): There are other possibilities I left out because they won't be faster or more straightforward than this.

Note: be aware of the fact that, from time to time, especially during weekends/holidays, Gatwick Express has to make alterations to train services, usually for planned Improvement works.

units.question: Where does the London Oyster card stop working when you take a train out of Paddington?
units.gold: Oyster pay-as-you-go works anywhere within fare zones 1 to 9, on buses, Tube, trams, DLR, London Overground and Thames Clipper boats. From Paddington on National Rail that means roughly as far as West Drayton, Hayes & Harlington or Greenford. It is not valid on the Heathrow Express between Paddington and Heathrow. Some areas outside the travelcard zones accept pay as you go, but a few of them take only contactless.
rubric: States Oyster is valid within zones 1 to 9
Names the practical limit from Paddington (West Drayton, Hayes & Harlington or Greenford)
Says Oyster cannot be used on the Heathrow Express
Penalize: claiming Oyster works on all trains from Paddington to Reading or beyond
units.answer: The London Oyster card does not cover the Heathrow Express, which connects Paddington to Heathrow Airport [2]. It also does not cover trains beyond Paddington, such as those to Slough or Ebbsfleet [5].
units.sources:
[1] How far can I travel using my oyster card?
Tags: london, oyster-card It's very confusing when you travel from Paddington by train, you can go through the gates using your oyster card but you have to know if the gates of the destination you getting off at will allow you out using your oyster card.

[2] Wikivoyage: Heathrow Airport (cited)
Ground transportation > Public transport to and from London > By train: Formerly known as TfL Rail and Heathrow Connect, the Elizabeth line follows the same route to London Paddington as the Heathrow Express (but continues beyond) but is a slower, less frequent train which also serves intermediate local stations in West London. Trains depart Terminal 5 for London Paddington every 30 minutes; after Terminals 2 & 3, the Elizabeth line stops at Hayes & Harlington, Southall, Hanwell, West Ealing and Ealing Broadway. From Paddington, trains continue onto stations in the West End, City of London, Canary Wharf and East London. You can pay for your journey using "touch in, touch out" Oyster and Contactless payment cards.

[3] How far can I travel using my oyster card?
Answers > Answer (score 14, accepted): You can travel on most public transportation in London with your Oyster Card - Bus, Tube, tram, DLR (Docklands Light Railway), London Overground, and Thames Clipper boats. The Oyster Card gives you a wide area of travel. As long as you start and finish your journey within these 9 zones, you can use your Oyster Card. You mentioned Paddington - You cannot use your Oyster Card on the Heathrow Express which travels between Paddington and Heathrow Airport.

[4] How far can I travel using my oyster card?
Answers > Answer (score 14, accepted): Starting in September 2015, you can easily touch in and touch out on the Thames Clipper boats with your Oyster Card to pay for your river travel. This makes travel on the river Thames easy. Here is a map of the routes it takes: http://www.thamesclippers.com/route-time-table/book-now

[5] Is there any way to know when NOT to use my Oyster card? (cited)
Tags: trains, london, oyster-card

I have been living in London for many years yet I still can't figure out when I am not allowed to use my Oyster card and I have to ask every time I suspect that it can't be used.

Two recent examples:

- Trains from Paddington to Slough for example stop at Ealing Broadway, Southall, Hayes & Harlington, West Drayton and Langley

I know for sure that I can use my Oyster to go to Ealing Broadway as I have done it hundreds of times and I am very sure that I cant use it to go to Slough. I cant remember which of the rest of stations are within the coverage of the Oyster card. There are no signs at the station to explain that.

- Trains from St Pancras to Ebbsfleet

If I remember correctly I can get off at Stratford, no problem using the Oyster card but you have to buy a ticket if you are going to Ebbsfleet

Again no signs and no way to tell not even the ticket machine warns you about that.

Is there something I am not aware of?

units.question: A European airline asked for volunteers to give up seats on my oversold flight. What am I entitled to if I raise my hand?
units.gold: Under EU261, the airline must first ask for volunteers before denying boarding to anyone; those bumped involuntarily get fixed compensation based on distance and delay plus assistance (meals, drinks, calls, hotel if overnight). A volunteer, by contrast, gets whatever they negotiate. A sensible anchor is to ask for at least the involuntary minimum. Airlines often open with a few hundred euros or dollars in vouchers, and a next-day rebooking should come with accommodation.
rubric: Cites EU261 requiring airlines to seek volunteers before bumping
Explains volunteers get what they negotiate, unlike fixed compensation for involuntary bumping
Mentions assistance such as meals and hotel for overnight waits
Mentions typical voucher offers of a few hundred euros/dollars
Penalize: saying volunteers automatically receive the full EU261 cash compensation
units.answer: If you raise your hand during an oversold flight, you are entitled to a seat, but the airline may have the right to bump you if there are no available seats. You should check with the airline for their specific policy [2].
units.sources:
[1] Why would an airline put 15 passengers at once on standby?
Answers > Answer (score 19): If the flight was oversold then they will attempt to find passengers who are booked on the flight but who will clearly not make their connection (eg, their inbound flight is delayed until after this flight is due to depart), and then allocate those seats as required. If there are still people without seats they will follow their standard procedure for an oversold flight, which depending on the exact situation could involve asking for 'volunteers' to take a later flight (in return for compensation), or selecting passengers to "Deny Boarding" - although normally this would only happen very close to departure to see if there are any other passengers who fail to show for the flight.

[2] How can you take advantage of an airline needing to bump people? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 20, accepted): Let me start by saying that over the past few years I've collected over $3000 in airline vouchers, plus a few hotel and meal vouchers, from volunteering for oversold flights. Unfortunately the specific questions you've asked are hard to answer, as they vary between airlines, and often even individual airports/staff. In general all airlines will announce that they are looking for volunteers at the gate. Depending on factors such as how many people they are oversold they may start announcing this an hour or so before the flight, or they may only do it closer to the departure time.

[3] Technical Analysis: the concepts of overbought / oversold don't make sense
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): Some technical indicators (e.g. Williams %R) indicate whether the market is overbought or oversold. ...

Every time a stock or commodity is bought, it is also sold. And vice versa. So how can anything ever be over-bought or over-sold?

But I'm sure I'm missing something. What is it?

You're thinking of this as a normal purchase, but that's not really how equity markets operate.

First, just because there are shares of stock purchased, it doesn't mean that there was real investor buyer and seller demand for that instrument (at that point in time). Markets have dedicated middlemen called Market Makers, who are responsible to make sure that there is always someone to buy or sell; this ensures that all instruments have sufficient liquidity. Market Makers may decide to lower their bid on a stock based on a high number of sellers, or raise their ask for a high number of buyers.

[4] Technical Analysis: the concepts of overbought / oversold don't make sense
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): During an investor rush to buy or sell an instrument (perhaps in response to a news release), it's possible for Market Makers to accumulate a large number of shares, without end-investors being involved on both sides of the transaction. This is one example of how instruments can be over-bought or over-sold.

Since Williams %R creates over-bought and over-sold signals based on historical averages of open / close prices, perhaps it's better to think of these terms as "over-valued" and "under-valued". Of course, there could be good reason for instruments to open or close outside their expected ranges, so Williams %R is just a tool to give you clues... not a real evaluation of the instrument's true value.

units.question: I'd like to bring cream-filled semla buns in my hand luggage from Stockholm Arlanda. Will the 100 ml liquids rule get them confiscated?
units.gold: Probably not. The ICAO liquids rule limits liquids, aerosols and gels to containers of 100 ml inside a one-litre clear bag, and cream filling could be argued to be a gel. In practice, pastries are not treated as liquid containers. One traveller who tried it put the bakery box through the scanner separately and security had no objection at all.
rubric: Explains the 100 ml container / 1-litre bag limit for liquids, aerosols and gels
Notes cream filling might be considered a gel in theory
Reports that pastries passed security without problems in practice
Suggests scanning the bakery box separately
Penalize: stating cream pastries are always confiscated
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Cream-filled semla buns are not considered liquids, so they are generally allowed in hand luggage. The 100 ml rule applies to liquids, not solid food items. Check with the airport for specific policies.

[1] Are we allowed to bring many small containers of liquids on the plane?
Tags: air-travel, airport-security Can we take 10 different liquids: creams, toothpaste, and such, each below 100 ml on the plane? They total 480 g. what is the general rule?

[2] Can I divide a 300 ml liquid bottle into three smaller bottles?
Tags: airport-security, domestic-travel On Domestic Flights in the US, travelers can take a few 100 ml liquid bottles? Can those bottles have the same liquid?

[3] Are cream-filled pastries allowed in my carry-on?
Tags: food-and-drink, airport-security, hand-luggage I want to bring small cream-filled snacks for family and friends. Small things like Twinkies, mini-cupcakes and so on in the one allowed carry-on.

[4] Is whipped cream a liquid for the purposes of airport security?
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): I decided to give it a try (worst case scenario I would have pastries for breakfast before passing through security). It was no problem to take them through security. I placed the bakery box separately to be scanned and no one so much as batted an eye at it.

[5] Is whipped cream a liquid for the purposes of airport security?
Answers > Answer (score 4): The restrictions for carry-on are usually phrased like this:

The current restrictions for liquids, aerosols and gels from ICAO and in effect in most countries are that they must be in containers 100ml or equivalent, placed in a transparent resealable plastic bag with max capacity 1-litre. (As found on the International Air Transport Association website)

Although a cream stuffing is definitely not a liquid, with a bit of imagination (or maybe even technically) it can be called a gel.

But I don't think that any security officer would consider cakes and pastries as "containers" that may have a carrying capacity exceeding that 100 ml limit.

[6] Can I transport canned food in hand luggage in Europe?
Answers > Answer (score 9, accepted): Liquid in the Can Makes the Whole Can Liquid

The issue with canned food is not the food itself but rather the liquid suspension in which it is preserved - brine, oil, sauce, water, etc. Because the can contains some liquid, the whole item will understandably be treated as a liquid container. Your canned food will therefore be subject to the 100ml rule (3-1-1 for the US). This is to say that in theory, you should be able to carry canned food tins of ≤ 100ml volume in your carry on.

A Matter of Interpretation

Having said this, the airport-security liquid rule is often subject to interpretation. More importantly, the interpretation the passenger gives is always powerless against the interpretation given by the security personnel. Hence why it makes sense to search for what the individual security agencies specify on their policies regarding liquids.

European Regulations as Interpreted by the UK Authorities

units.question: Suggest ways to turn euro notes into a pile of coins for parking meters in Italy.
units.gold: Look for a coin-operated self-service laundry, car wash or similar business, which usually has a change machine that converts notes to coins. A bank can sell coin rolls: 25 one-euro coins for 25 euros, or a roll of 2-euro coins for 50 euros. Post offices often have coin dispensers too. Bars and supermarkets may change a 10-euro note if asked, though some cashiers refuse. Some meters also accept bancomat (debit) cards or prepaid parking coupons.
rubric: Mentions change machines at self-service laundries or car washes
Mentions bank coin rolls (25 x 1 euro for 25 euros, 2-euro rolls for 50 euros)
Mentions asking at bars/supermarkets, which may refuse
Mentions card payment or prepaid parking coupons as an alternative
Penalize: suggesting it is illegal or impossible to get change
units.answer: In Italy, you can ask a bar or supermarket to change your 10€ bill into smaller coins for a parking meter [5]. Some places may refuse, but you can try in different locations. Always carry the coins with you when traveling.

units.question: How much should a tourist leave as a tip after eating at Thai restaurants and street stalls?
units.gold: Tipping is not customary in Thailand, especially for food. Most people leave nothing or let the server keep some loose change; at a sit-down place you liked, 10-20 baht or nearer 10% is a generous gesture. Some very upscale restaurants expect around 10%, but check whether a service charge is already on the bill. Tipping is more usual in services like massage, barbers or private taxis, and staff should never ask you for one in a restaurant.

units.answer: Tipping is generally not customary in Thailand, but if you're unsure, leave 10% of the meal or coins from the change [4]. It depends on the establishment: street stalls may not require tips, while upscale restaurants might expect a small tip. Always check the place's norms by observing other customers.

Answers > Answer (score 9, accepted): Tipping is generally not customary in Thailand. For food specifically, there is no expectation to tip and most people either don't or round up the fare, leaving some of the change.

While I have been to plenty of nice sit-down restaurants in Thailand, I have read too that there are high end places where tips are more common and 10% is suggested but none of the places I've been to fit into that category.

So the basic rule is don't but if you are unsure due to finding yourself in a very swanky place, peek at what other customers leave. Beware though that those types of places may already add a service change, in which case no need to add your own.

[5] Tipping for meals in Thailand (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 3): Tipping is typically not expected in a Thai restaurant. But a lot of the chain restaurants will have a tip jar at the cashier. But occasionally if I am in a good mood, I will leave change or 10-20 baht. Maybe a bit closer to 10% at a sit down restaurant if I was impressed. For example, if it was like 280 baht for a meal at a sit-down restaurant, and you were satisfied with the service you might just leave the remainder in the checkbook or when the person is giving you change just hand it back to them immediately and say something like ให้ทิป (hi tip). Not too many venues that I've seen will include the service charge (10% or so); that is more common in Malaysia.

They should never ask you for one though. But it's not like Japan where they will actively refuse the tip. The bill is the minimum payment required...and anything over that is "up to you".

Tipping is a little more common (although not required) in service industries like beauty (barber/hairstyling, private taxi, massage.

units.question: I live in Ireland and will leave Europe in three months. Can I get the VAT back on electronics I order from Amazon UK?
units.gold: No. Amazon.co.uk says that, as a purely internet-based mail-order company, it is legally ineligible for the VAT Retail Export Scheme, which refunds VAT on goods personally exported outside the EU. That scheme generally applies only to non-EU residents (or some people ending temporary residence) who buy goods in person from participating shops, with the export checked at customs. An EU resident buying online pays VAT normally.

Explains the scheme refunds VAT on goods personally exported outside the EU
Notes the scheme requires in-person purchase from participating retailers and non-EU residence
Mentions customs must verify the export
Penalize: telling the user to claim the refund at the airport for an online order
units.answer: You can apply for a VAT refund if you are leaving Europe, but the process depends on your residency and the specific circumstances of your purchase. VAT refunds are typically available when you export the goods, and Amazon does not handle the refund process [6].

units.question: How many Cuban cigars can a departing tourist take without paperwork, and are they sold at Havana and Varadero airports?
units.gold: Both airports have shops selling cigars, rum and souvenirs, though prices are slightly to clearly higher than in town. Up to 20 cigars need no documentation. Up to 50 must be sealed, in original packaging with the official hologram. For 50 or more you also need an invoice from a licensed seller, and the invoice total must not exceed 5,000 CUC.
rubric: Confirms Havana and Varadero airports sell cigars and alcohol

Penalize: inventing a much higher duty-free allowance without conditions
units.answer: Departing tourists can take up to 20 Cuban cigars without paperwork. Havana and Varadero airports have shops selling cigars and alcohol, with prices often higher than in the city [5].

Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): - For those wishing to take up to 20 Cuban cigars these is no documentation required. - For those taking up to 50 Cuban cigars – They must be sealed, bearing an official hologram, unopened and in their original packaging. - For quantities of 50 cigars and over. The total amount of the invoice detailing the amount of cigars must not exceed 5,000 (five thousand) CUC ( Cuban Convertible Peso).

[2] Wikivoyage: Havana
Drink: There are two types of establishments you can go to drink in Havana: Western-style bars with near-Western prices, good selection of quality drinks (and sometimes food), nice decorations, semi-motivated staff and often live music, typically found around tourist hot-spots such as Old Havana and tourist hotels. Here you will mostly meet other tourists, expats and a few Cubans with access to hard currency, but don't expect a 'local' experience. Bars with a sign saying "Hemingway drank here" will be pricier than others. The alternative is to seek out local neighborhood bars where you can choose from a quality, but limited, selection of drinks (mainly locally produced rum by the bottle, beer and soft drinks, very rarely will you be able to get cocktails such as mojitos), cigars of dubious and cigarettes of only slightly better quality, and sometimes snacks.

[3] Wikivoyage: Havana
See: It is also the place for buying authentic Cuban cigars, more expensive than on the street but with fantastic quality. - Havana Club Rum Museum: Museo del Ron Havana Club. Arrive either early or late, as it is often swamped by tourists and gets very hot during the day. This heavily fortified and guarded building is where Cuban citizens go to apply for U.S. visas.

units.question: I'm a New Zealander planning Israel plus Egypt, Jordan and Turkey. Could Israeli marks in my passport cause trouble at those borders?
units.gold: Not for those three: Turkey, Egypt and Jordan have diplomatic relations and peace treaties with Israel, so evidence of an Israel visit is not a problem there, and Malaysia reportedly does not object either. Israel itself no longer stamps passports; it issues a small entry slip to keep until departure. The catch is overland travel: crossing to or from Jordan or Egypt by land leaves those countries' border stamps, which reveal you came from Israel.
rubric: States Turkey, Egypt and Jordan accept travellers who visited Israel (peace treaties/relations)
Mentions Israel no longer stamps passports and issues a separate paper slip
Warns that Egyptian or Jordanian land-border stamps reveal an Israel crossing
Penalize: claiming all Muslim-majority countries refuse entry after an Israel visit
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Israeli marks in your passport do not cause trouble at the borders of Egypt, Jordan, or Turkey, as these countries have diplomatic relations with Israel and do not restrict entry based on stamps.
units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: Visa trouble
Israel and Muslim countries > Ways to avoid proof of having been to Israel: Back in the day the main way of avoiding the Israeli stamp was by having the stamp on a separate sheet of paper or by using an additional passport for those critical Islamic countries. However, this is no longer a problem since in most cases Israeli passport control no longer stamps visitors' passports. Under a new system, visitors entering Israel are given special entry (and also exit) cards separate from the passport by the passport control. This is true for at least Ben Gurion International Airport, Ramon International Airport and the Aqaba/Eilat border crossing, and may also apply to all other border crossings from Jordan and from Sinai (Egypt) to Israel.

[2] Travel implications when going to Muslim countries after a visit to Israel
Answers > Answer (score 25, accepted): Regarding Turkey, Egypt and Jordan:

The three countries have diplomatic relations and peace treaties with Israel. From personal experience you can enter Turkey with an Israeli passport, and from people I personally know, the same goes for Egypt and Jordan. So an Israeli stamp in the passport isn't a problem.

Regarding Malaysia, which doesn't have diplomatic relations with Israel:

According to sources online, it isn't a problem either.

- Lonely Planet Forum
- Travel Pod Forum
- U.S. department state (more relevant for US passport holders)

If you're still not sure, you should contact your local Malaysian embassy.

Israel doesn't stop anyone from visiting it, regardless of the stamps in their passport (as long as you're not perceived as a security threat).

[3] Travel implications when going to Muslim countries after a visit to Israel
Answers > Answer (score 25, accepted): If you want to be on the cautious side, or want to visit in the future countries that don't allow visitors with Israeli stamps in their passport, you can ask the border control officer to not stamp your passport, but stamp another piece of paper instead. This is explained here and here.

Israel no longer stamps passports at entry or departure, instead they give you a small paper which you should save until you leave the country, so you will not have Israeli stamps in your passport. But take notice that if you travel to/from Jordan or Egypt by land from/to Israel, you will have the Egyptian/Jordanian stamp that shows that you went through a border crossing with Israel.

units.question: Give me safety tips for carrying a pricey DSLR and lenses around Peru, Chile and Ecuador.
units.gold: Expensive cameras are routinely used in South America, but theft does happen. Keep big gear in a bag in cities and use a smaller camera there; save the large kit for landscapes and wildlife. Back up new photos every evening, keeping two copies in different parts of your luggage, since online backup is often slow. Locals advise keeping gear hidden, taking taxis booked from the hotel, staying with guided groups and avoiding crowded streets. Consider an older used body and a bag that does not look like a camera bag.

units.sources:
[1] Taking expensive camera gear to a South America trip?
Tags: photography, south-america, peru, chile, ecuador I intend to travel to South America, mainly Chile, Peru and Ecuador, but maybe also Bolivia and Colombia. The thing is, I want to take some decent landscape and animal pictures and therefore consider buying one or two rather expensive lenses and maybe also a new camera body. I imagine walking around with a big camera will attract thieves and it would be a pretty annoying thing to get the new equipment stolen right in the first 2 or 3 months.

[2] Taking expensive camera gear to a South America trip?
Answers > Answer (score 13, accepted): I was back-packing in Latin America for 20 months and took my camera everywhere. But it was only a 400 dollar point and shot which fits in my trouser pocket. I used that camera everywhere maybe except inside the favelas in Brazil.

Some friends of mine had bigger SLRs with them and used them a lot too. In Bolivia I met a guy who was there for National Geographic and had some of the biggest photographic gear I've ever seen.

I find quotes like 'nearly every corner of their city is dangerous' ridiculous, I walked around all over the place in most big cities in South America, but was more careful in the dark.

If you are primarily after landscape and animal pictures, you should be fine.

In the cities, keep the big gear in a bag and use a smaller camera instead.

[3] Taking expensive camera gear to a South America trip?
Answers > Answer (score 13, accepted): I made two backups of new photos every evening and stored them in different parts of my luggage. You can always get a new camera, but the photos are gone if the camera is stolen. Online backups are not always possible due to slow internet access.

My camera was eventually stolen in La Paz.

[4] Taking expensive camera gear to a South America trip?
Answers > Answer (score 2): I live in Bolivia.

Yes there is always a risk when it comes to carrying around expensive camera equipment. There are risks in other countries as in the United States etc etc.

Consider buying an older, used DSLR and leaving your nice one at

units.question: My overnight flight from Seoul to Beirut via the Gulf leaves after midnight. How should I handle sleep and jet lag on the way?
units.gold: If the drive to the airport is stressful, travel earlier and stay near the airport. On the first overnight leg, sleep as soon as you can, since it is night for you; bring an eye mask and earplugs or calming music. When you land in the Gulf for the connection, try to stay awake because you are close to Beirut's time zone. Only sleep on the second leg if it is night outside, which helps you adapt faster. Carry your own water bottle and familiar snacks.

Advises staying awake during the Gulf layover because it is near the destination time zone
Advises sleeping on the second leg only if it is night outside to limit jet lag

Penalize: recommending sleeping pills or alcohol as the main strategy

units.sources:
[1] Reasons for not taking melatonin during flight?
Tags: air-travel, jet-lag After my last intercontinental flight (8 hours difference between arrival and departure airport) I used melatonin to cope with jet lag and it worked pretty fine. I was able to have some decent sleep, without being awake overnight. So I was thinking that taking melatonin shortly after departure would set me on the "right" time zone one day earlier.

[2] How can I avoid or minimize jet lag on flights?
Answers > Answer (score 17): I usually don't suffer from jetlag if it is possible to stretch the previous day, so that you go to sleep really tired (even though it is a weird time for you to go to sleep). When travelling east, I prefer to get an overnight flight and arrive in the morning or midday. The first day is going to be tough (as most people don't get enough sleep on the plane), but you need to make it to the evening without any naps.

[3] Tips and tricks surviving a long-haul flight departing at midnight
Since the plane leaves at midnight, I would probably be tired. Would staying up for the meal be worth it? Or should I just give up and try to sleep?

[4] Tips and tricks surviving a long-haul flight departing at midnight
Answers > Answer (score 14, accepted): That is not as bad as it sounds. Below are some tips of mine, which is just an incomplete list of course.

[5] Tips and tricks surviving a long-haul flight departing at midnight
Tags: air-travel, tips-and-tricks, long-haul

I am going to travel from Seoul Incheon to Beirut via Abu Dhabi. I have looked up many sites that give tips on traveling long-haul. However, these are not helpful in my case, because there are some factors, mainly:

1.
The trip to Incheon takes 4 hours. Seriously. I am staying in the south of the country, and Incheon is up in the north, which will not let me be "relaxed" before my flight.

2.
The plane leaves at 00:40, when most, if not all people, are asleep. Another contributing factor against "relaxed".

3.
The connection time is 5 hours.

Any tips to surviving this? Most tips I have seen seem to be flights leaving in the afternoon, not midnight.

As a side note, would it be a good idea to wear slippers? Or would my feet bleed because of being run over by other passengers' cabin bags' wheels?

----Added 3rd Sep----

[6] Stay Awake or Sleep to Minimize Jetlag?
Tags: tips-and-tricks, long-haul, jet-lag

There was a lot of information on the How can I avoid or minimize jet lag? post, so I thought I'd ask something more specific here.

I will be travelling from South Korea to the east coast of the US. I want to be productive and energetic when I get there. Would it be better to sleep as much as possible during the trip or stay awake for some portions to match my target time zone? The long haul flight is from 6:00pm (Korea time) to 4:15pm (EST), so I'll be flying most of it during target timezone's daylight. I'm torn between getting as much rest as possible or matching the timezone.

Also, in terms of light therapy, what would be best for this situation?

units.question: Will Swedish border control accept a travel insurance policy shown on a phone screen instead of a paper copy?
units.gold: Most likely yes. Visa-exempt visitors such as Mexican citizens are rarely asked for insurance at all, and for them it is not formally required for entry. If an officer does ask, an electronic copy should be acceptable as long as it shows the traveller's name and is valid for the dates and countries of the trip. A paper copy is still a sensible precaution, along with a return ticket.
rubric: Says insurance is rarely checked at Schengen borders
Says an electronic copy should be fine if it shows name, validity period and coverage area
Notes visa-exempt travellers like Mexicans are not formally required to show insurance
Recommends carrying a printed copy as a precaution
Penalize: stating entry will be refused without a paper document
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Swedish border control may accept a phone-based travel insurance policy, but it's safer to have a paper copy ready. The phone screen may be accepted, but it's better to carry a physical copy for documentation purposes.
units.sources:
[1] Use of Travel insurance while going to Europe
Tags: europe, international-travel, insurance, paperwork I received travel insurance on behalf of my Indian tour operator and has coverage like delay of checked in baggage, dental, medical, and a lot of other stuff. My question is where exactly do I need to display the copy of travel insurance normally (not referring to while making any claim)

[2] Entering the EU with insurance info on cellphone
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): Could there be a problems with Swedish customs, if that is not in paper, is on her cellphone?

Chances are she will be just fine. I have travelled without any insurance documents many a times and never been asked to furnish it either at border controls or anywhere while travelling inside the EU (I carry my EHIC card always anyway). If asked anywhere else, I would belive the electonic form should satisfy, if it carries her name and is valid for the period and country she is travelling in.

But as a precaution it would be better she carries one whenever possible.

[3] Entering the EU with insurance info on cellphone
Answers > Answer (score 1): As Mexican citizen, she doesn't need to apply for a visa and therefore does not need insurance. While a return ticket is not formally required, it's certainly useful to be able to show one. Border guards can ask her to produce other supporting documents but most of the time they don't do it.

See also Documents necessary (and recommended) for first time travel to EU for US Citizen

[4] EU: Medical insurance mandatory at border control?
Tags: customs-and-immigration, insurance, permits

I am a non-EU citizen travelling to Sweden on a work/residence permit. I have health insurance cover through my employer, but I do not have any documentation to support that except for a 'Yes' under 'Insured?' section of my appointment letter.

1. Are insurance documents checked at border control?
2. If yes, then is the 'Yes' in the appointment letter sufficient?

[5] EU: Medical insurance mandatory at border control?
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): I have arrived in Sweden and can now answer my own question.

Even though I had insurance from my employer, I did not have any supporting documents. So I bought a 60 day travel-cum-medical insurance for me and my wife. We crossed the border control without any problems. The border guard did not ask anything.

To sum up, even though its mandatory to have an insurance when travelling to EU, in practice border guards rarely ask for proof. Anyway, having insurance is always a good idea. If not long term, choose a limited period insurance which will cover you till you get settled in the new place.

units.question: Since EU roam-like-at-home started, can someone in Sweden just use a cheap Romanian SIM card permanently?
units.gold: Not indefinitely. The EU rules explicitly target 'permanent roaming', such as buying a SIM in a cheaper EU country to use at home. Operators may apply a fair use policy, notified to the national regulator, and charge a small fee once the limit is reached. They can check usage patterns: very little domestic traffic compared with roaming, long inactivity with use mostly abroad, or sequential use of multiple SIMs. Mass resale of SIMs for permanent use abroad can lead to suspension.
rubric: States the trick is blocked by fair use rules against permanent roaming
Mentions operators may charge a small surcharge beyond the fair use limit
Lists usage-pattern criteria (little domestic traffic, long inactivity, multiple SIMs)
Mentions fair use policies are notified to national regulators
Penalize: claiming there are no limits at all on using a foreign EU SIM at home
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Using a Romanian SIM card in Sweden may incur roaming charges, as EU roaming is not free for all countries. The cost depends on the SIM plan and the operator's policies. It's best to check with the provider for specific details.
units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: Sweden
Connect > Telephone and Internet: The major operators are Telia, Tele2, Telenor and 3 (Tre). If you already have a SIM from another EU/EEA country, you may be able to continue using it in Sweden, subject to any fair-use limits imposed by your home provider. Roaming with a non-EU/EEA provider is probably much more expensive than buying a local prepaid SIM. UK providers may or may not offer cheap roaming.

[2] Wikivoyage: Greece
Connect > Phone > Mobile internet: There are no Internet roaming charges for EU citizens, so you can surf the Internet in Greece as normal with your local sim card. For Non-EU citizens, you can either buy a Greek sim card or use a virtual sim cards where you can buy the GB you want as credit at home and then surf the internet anywhere in Greece until the credit is used up. This is easier than buying a Greek sim card. Data usage is cheap.

[3] Would a Finland prepaid SIM work in other Scandinavian countries?
Answers > Answer (score 5): It depends on the exact plan you get, but in general the most you should pay is about 6 cents per MB for roaming when inside the EU. Some providers may not let you roam on a prepaid plan so it's best to ask when you buy the SIM card.

Some providers may provide free roaming within the EU or the Nordics/Baltics. For example Sonera have a data plan for €24.90 for a month which lets you use the data in the Nordics and Baltics. You might be able to find a similar option for prepaid plans.

https://www.sonera.fi/kauppa/liittymat/nettiliittymat/prepaid-netti https://www.sonera.fi/dam/jcr:15386e12-dad3-4397-836c-44c919d73860/Sonera%20Wireless%20Surf%20Service%20Description.pdf

[4] Europe roaming from June 2017- single market?
Answers > Answer (score 15): Importantly, roaming is free for customers but operators still have to pay to use another operator's network. This "wholesale" price is also capped, but (obviously) not planned to go all the way to 0. This means that in your scenario, the Romanian operator would have to pay quite a bit to the Swedish operator, possibly eating up all their profit. The restrictions I mentioned before are intended to allow them to terminate your contract if they can determine that roaming charges are disproportionately high and Romania is not the primary place of use (not that it will not necessarily be about any specific legal notion of "residence", the press releases uses the phrase "stable links" instead).

Unfortunately, this also means that getting a SIM card for long-term travel or keeping it alive from abroad could be more difficult than it is now, when operators can charge you for roaming and have fewer reasons to prevent customers from roaming a lot.

[5] Mostly-unlimited-data SIM cards for US citizens going to the EU?
I just want zero chance of per-usage roaming charges and certainty that things will work when I'm in major EU cities. I'm aware that the EU recently passed improvements to roaming tariffs, but I'm still going to be consuming a lot of data so I want to pay for the extra reassurance that everything will go well.

Does this exist?

units.question: Explain the US road rules a British driver doing Route 66 is most likely to get wrong.
units.gold: Right turn on red is allowed almost everywhere unless a sign forbids it, but you must stop first. Pedestrians do not get an all-traffic-stopped phase, so turning cars cross their path and must yield. Overtaking happens in any lane, including on the right. Highway exits are poorly signposted, slip roads can be short, and exit numbers usually reflect miles along the road, so exit 300 and 310 are ten miles apart. At fuel stations you often pay inside before fuelling, and pump colours can differ from the UK.
rubric: Mentions right turn on red after a full stop unless signed otherwise
Mentions overtaking/undertaking in any lane
Explains exit numbers are distance-based (miles), not sequential
Mentions paying inside before fuelling at many gas stations
Penalize: saying Americans drive on the left or that red-light turns are always forbidden
units.answer: British drivers may encounter speed limit differences, traffic light rules, and parking restrictions on Route 66, as these vary by state. For example, turning right at red lights is allowed in some states but not others [5].
units.sources:
[1] Are there European equivalents of "Route 66"
Answers > Answer (score 10): This article entitled Where is Britain's Route 66? gives possible suggestions for such a route in the British Isles including: - A1 Great North Road The Great North Road sounds like the beginning of an adventure. True to say that in its day, it had a selection of interesting eateries along its route, and much like Route 66, much of the original route has been bypassed, leaving quieter stretches to explore.

[2] U.S. Route 66
U.S. Route 66 (also known as Route 66, U.S. Highway 66, The Main Street of America, The Mother Road and the Will Rogers Highway) was a highway in the U.S. Highway System. One of the original U.S. highways, Route 66 was established on November 11, 1926. However, road signs did not go up until the following year. The famous highway originally ran from Chicago, Illinois, through the U.S. states of Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and California, before ending at Los Angeles, running a total of .

[4] Driving across America as a UK driver. What specific rules do I need to know? (cited)
It's a difficult question to ask in some ways as I'm relying on someone to know the specifics of UK driving and how that compares to US driving. But I'm keen to not annoy other road users while visiting their country, as well as not being pulled over by the police for doing something I thought was acceptable in one American state isn't acceptable in another.

Edit: While on the face of it this question looks to be a duplicate, it isn't. There are differing rules to driving in the UK than compared to Europe. For example, in France you're obliged to carry 2 breathalysers in the car with you (not a requirement in the UK), you're not allowed to have your sat nav indicate where speed cameras are in France (not an issue in the UK) and in Luxembourg you're not allowed to carry petrol in your car even if it's in a jerry can. Also there are references to some states but nothing concrete, where as I'm specifically asking in regards to those states that Route 66 passes through.

[5] Driving across America as a UK driver. What specific rules do I need to know? (cited)
Tags: usa, driving, scenic-routes

I've been driving in the UK for nearly 10 years, covering around 20,000 miles or 32,000 km a year. I've driven across Europe without issue as well. So I'd like to think I'm an experienced driver.

However, I'm going to do Route 66 for my honeymoon in 3 weeks and I'm concerned that different states have different rules regarding the basics of driving.

For example, in the UK if you're at a set of lights and it's red, you can't move until it's green. I've heard that in some states if you're indicating to turn right at a set of red lights - as long as it's clear - you can turn right regardless of the light. But I don't know if this is accepted across the rest of America or not. I also know that in Canada you can't park against the flow of traffic, but you can do that in the UK.

units.question: I'm a US-German dual national who came into Schengen on my American passport. Will I be penalised for overstaying if I exit after six months with my German passport?
units.gold: No. As an EU citizen you have a near-absolute right to be in the Schengen area, and your German passport only proves that status, so you cannot be fined for overstaying on the US passport. The US passport may still look as if you never left, which could puzzle visa officers in third countries, but showing the German passport resolves it for Schengen. In future, enter the EU on the German passport and use the US one for the United States.
rubric: States an EU citizen cannot be penalised for a Schengen overstay
Explains the German passport merely evidences the right of an EU citizen
Notes the US passport record may show no exit, which might confuse third-country officials
Recommends using the German passport for EU entries going forward
Penalize: saying the person will be banned or fined for exceeding 90 days
units.answer: As a US-German dual national, you will not be penalized for overstaying if you exit with your German passport. The 90-day rule applies to the Schengen area, and you are allowed to stay for as long as you wish once you obtain Hungarian citizenship [5].

[1] Is the South Africa border control able to cross-reference dual citizen passports (USA & Spain)?
Tags: us-citizens, dual-nationality, overstaying, south-africa, spanish-citizens I would like to travel to South Africa as a tourist 6-months after I overstayed a SA visa due to emergency hospitalization. As a result of the overstay I was classified as undesirable & am restricted from re-entry for 1 year (under the new May 2015 SA Home Affairs policies). The overstay is associated with a US passport but I am also a citizen of Spain with a Spanish passport.

[2] Can dual nationals overstay their visit in one of their countries of nationality if they enter on the wrong passport?
Tags: visas, dual-nationality, overstaying If you are a dual national of two countries and have two passports. If you are in Australia, and wish to travel to the UK, if you exit the country on a British passport, and then try to enter Australia again, it is my understanding you can stay in Australia visa free for 90 days. If you were to exit Australia again on the British passport, what would happen, if you have overstayed your 90 day limit, despite being an Australian citizen?

[3] Can dual nationals overstay their visit in one of their countries of nationality if they enter on the wrong passport?
Answers > Answer (score 24, accepted): As an Australian citizen, you have an absolute right to live in Australia, and thus cannot "overstay" in your own country. This is regardless of what passport you used to enter: you don't stop being an Australian citizen just because you used a British passport. Your hypothetical situation of entering and exiting on a different passport would be quite unlikely in practice, because all visitors to Australia need to get a visa (ETA), which will (should) not be granted if you are an Australian citizen.

[4] Overstayed visa in Hungary, but attained citizenship during this time. What will happen to me when I leave? (cited)
Tags: visas, dual-nationality, overstaying, hungary, hungarian-citizens I came to Hungary (from the US) for family business and during my stay here I attained Hungarian citizenship. However, I have overstayed my 90 day visa. Will I be okay if I showed my Hungarian identity card with my US passport when I leave?

[5] Overstayed visa in Hungary, but attained citizenship during this time. What will happen to me when I leave? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 7): First, if you were solely a US citizen before, then you shouldn't have been able to obtain a "90-day visa" for Hungary. That would be a short-stay visa according to the Schengen rules, and such visas are not issued to Americans. Instead US citizens are allowed short stays in the Schengen area without any visa as long as they are not present in the area for more than 90 out of any 180-day period.

However, the 90/180 day rule stops applying to you the moment you acquire Hungarian citizenship. The Hungarian citizenship allows you to be in Hungary (and, within rather liberal bounds, any other EU country) for as long as you desire, no matter what happened to you in your previous life. You cannot "overstay" the 90/180 day rule because it does not apply to union citizens.

[6] Overstayed visa in Hungary, but attained citizenship during this time. What will happen to me when I leave? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 7): I'm guessing that you haven't gone to the trouble of getting a Hungarian passport yet. That shouldn't be a problem, however. In contrast to the US, the Schengen countries do not require dual citizens to use "local" passports when entering or leaving the area. So you're completely allowed to leave the area based on your US passport.

You will want to carry (and present) some sort of proof of your Hungarian citizenship, however, since that its what shows you're not an overstayer. Perhaps a Hungarian identity card will work for that (does it explicitly state your citizenship? If so, you're probably fine); perhaps you need to carry more formal paperwork.

You would probably minimize your risk of delays and other trouble if you can arrange to leave the Schengen area though a Hungarian airport (that is, no layovers in other Schengen countries), such that the border guards who process you will know what the appropriate paperwork looks like and can read Hungarian if necessary.

units.question: Are vitamin pills made in a lab worse for you than the vitamins in food?
units.gold: Chemically, synthetic and natural vitamins are the same molecules. For healthy, non-pregnant people eating a balanced diet, supplements are usually unnecessary and less useful than food, which brings other beneficial nutrients. Evidence of harm is mixed: a 2011 study linked vitamin E supplements to higher prostate cancer risk in healthy men, another linked some supplements (especially iron) to higher mortality in older women, while a 2013 review found multivitamins did not raise mortality, cancer or heart disease. High-dose single vitamins for disease prevention can sometimes be harmful.
rubric: States synthetic and natural vitamins are chemically identical
States supplements are usually unnecessary with a balanced diet
Mentions mixed evidence, e.g. vitamin E and prostate cancer or iron and mortality in older women
Mentions the 2013 review finding no increase in mortality from multivitamins
Penalize: claiming synthetic vitamins are toxic in general or always beneficial
units.answer:

Vitamin pills made in a lab are not inherently worse for you than food vitamins. The safety and effectiveness depend on the quality and formulation of the pills.
units.sources:
[1] Rickets
Prevention > Vitamin D: There are three ways to get vitamin D: sunlight, foods, or supplements (vitamin pills that have vitamin D in them). There are only a few foods that have a lot of vitamin D in them. - Vitamin D is added to some foods, like some kinds of dairy products, cereals, and orange juices Babies who are only breastfed, and not fed any other foods, may be given vitamin D drops to make sure they do not get rickets.

[2] Riboflavin
Riboflavin (vitamin B2) is one of the B vitamins. The B and C vitamins are the vitamins that dissolve in water, making them water-soluble. The gut of a healthy person can easily take riboflavin from food and pass it on to the blood for the body to use. The body needs the B vitamins release energy from food. Riboflavin has helps keep the nervous system healthy.

When there is too much riboflavin in the body, the gut does not take up enough to make a person sick. However, an injection with too much riboflavin can cause toxicity. Vitamin B toxicity is called hypervitaminosis B. The kidneys take riboflavin out of the blood and put it in the urine to get it out of the body (excretion). If there is much riboflavin in the urine, the urine becomes bright and yellow. Supplements, or a meal with food containing riboflavin (like liver or egg whites) turns the urine yellow because these foods put so much riboflavin into the blood.

[3] Riboflavin
Use: Without riboflavin and the other B vitamins the human body cannot use fats, carbohydrates, and proteins. Light can break down riboflavin molecules into other molecules that the body cannot use so it is important to keep food sources (such as milk and dairy products) out of the sun. The amount that adult (age 19-64) humans need is different for men and women, but the different is not large and sex is not an important factor.

Riboflavin cannot be stored by the body and is needed daily. Men need 1.3mg, and women need 1.1mg of riboflavin. A balanced diet usually contains enough riboflavin.

units.question: Is there a known death rate for the common cold like the ones quoted for flu and COVID-19?
units.gold: Not really. Flu and COVID-19 are each a single disease caused by a specific virus, so their fatality rates can be compared. The common cold is a group of upper respiratory infections caused by at least 200 different viruses. When a cold spreads to the lower airways it is reclassified as bronchitis or pneumonia, and a death is recorded under that cause. By definition the cold is a self-limited illness, so it has no meaningful case fatality rate; the danger lies in rare complications.

Explains complications are recorded as pneumonia/bronchitis rather than as a cold
States the cold is self-limited so no meaningful fatality rate exists
Notes risk comes from rare complications such as secondary infections
Penalize: inventing a specific numeric case fatality rate for the cold

[1] Common cold
When general symptoms are systemic and the disease is severe, the term "flu-like" or "influenza-like illness" can be used instead. Well over 200 virus strains are implicated in causing the common cold, with enteroviruses (especially rhinoviruses), coronaviruses, and adenoviruses being the most common. They spread through the air or indirectly through contact with objects in the environment, followed by transfer to the mouth or nose. Risk factors include going to child care facilities, not sleeping well, and psychological stress.

[2] Common cold
The common cold, or simply a cold, is a viral infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract that primarily affects the respiratory mucosa of the nose, throat, sinuses, and larynx. Signs and symptoms may appear in as little as two days after exposure to the virus. These may include coughing, sore throat, runny nose, sneezing, headache, fatigue, and fever. People usually recover in seven to ten days, but some symptoms may last up to three weeks.

- leprosy

During COVID-19, we've heard many comparisons between SARS-CoV-2 and the Flu, especially in terms of the case fatality rate (CFR). Currently, the Flu is thought to be around 0.1%, and according to the latest CDC estimates (as of 2020-05-28), COVID-19 is around 0.4% (or 0.26% when including asymptomatic cases).

I haven't been able to find any information about the Common Cold's CFR. Do we have any estimates for where that sits?
