units.question: Why can't a bitcoin public key be recovered from the address it belongs to?
units.gold: An address is a hash of the public key, using SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160, which are one-way functions. The address is also only 160 bits while the public key is about 257 bits, so information is simply missing. Bitcoin uses the short hash to keep addresses compact. When coins sent to the address are spent, the spender must reveal the public key so nodes can hash it, match the address and verify the signature; from then on the key is public.
rubric: States the address is a hash (SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160) of the public key
Explains hashes are one-way functions
Mentions the size difference (160-bit address vs ~257-bit key)
Says the public key becomes visible when the address first spends
Penalize: claiming the address is the public key itself
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
A Bitcoin public key cannot be recovered from the address it belongs to because the address itself is a hash of the public key, and the public key is not stored anywhere publicly. The address is designed to be unique and cannot be reversed to reveal the original key.
units.sources:
[1] Bitcoin
Pseudonymous: The public key, which is what the "bitcoin address" is created from, is similar to an email address; anyone can look it up and send bitcoins to it. The private address, or private key, is similar to an email password; only with it can the owner send bitcoins from it. To send bitcoins from an address, you prove to the network that you own the private key that belongs to the address, without revealing the private key. This is done with a branch of mathematics known as public-key cryptography.

[2] Bitcoin
Pseudonymous > Public key: A public key is what determines the ownership of bitcoins, and is very similar to an ID number. If someone wanted to send you bitcoins, all you would need to do is supply them your bitcoin address, which is a version of your public key that is easier to read and type. For example, if Bob has 1 bitcoin at the bitcoin address "ABC123," and Alice has no bitcoins at the bitcoin address "DEF456," Bob can send 0.5 bitcoins to "DEF456." Anyone using the system can see how much money "ABC123" has and how much money "DEF456" has, but they cannot tell anything about who owns the address.

[3] How can I speculatively invest $1000 in (micro)bitcoin?
Answers > Answer (score 4): 1. Use the software/service to create a new wallet (which is just two long codes: Your public wallet address and your secret wallet key). When you lose it, there is no way to recover your bitcoins. Pay $1000 in exchange for a bitcoin payment to your wallet address.

[4] Bitcoin BIPs: BIP 179: Name for payment recipient identifiers
Rationale: The reason why we use Bitcoin Invoice Address or just Invoice is to emphasize that it is single-use. The terms Bitcoin and Address are optional for the following reasons: - Useful for multicoin wallets to indicate that it belongs to Bitcoin - Bitcoin Invoice Address

[5] How can I speculatively invest $1000 in (micro)bitcoin?
Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): Find a (reputable) exchange that accepts business from citizens of the country you re located in and purchase through them.

Be advised though that fear of missing out and investing in something you dont even know how is called (let alone understand) can be a very bad practice and sets you up for losses.

[6] Bitcoin
Pseudonymous > Private key: In the example above, "ABC123" and "DEF456" are the bitcoin addresses of Bob and Alice. But Bob and Alice each have a second key which only they individually know. This is the private key, and it is the "other half" of a Bitcoin address. The private key is never shared, and allows the owner of the bitcoins to control them. However, if the private key is not kept secret, then anyone who sees it can also control and take the bitcoins there. This happened on live TV when Bloomberg's Matt Miller accidentally showed a private key to viewers. The money was taken immediately. The person who took it, told others about it later, saying "I'll send it back once Matt gives me a new address, since someone else can sweep [empty] out the old one."

[7] Key exchange
The key exchange problem is how to exchange whatever keys or other information needed so, in such a way, that no one else can obtain a copy. Usually, this required trusted secure channel. With the arrival of (public key / private key) cipher algorithms, the encrypting key (aka, the public key) could be made public, since (at least for "high quality" ciphers) no one without the decrypting key (aka, the private key) could decrypt the message.

In principle, then, the only remaining problem was to be sure that a public key actually belonged to its claimed owner, this is not a problem easy to solve; specially when the two users involved have never met and know nothing about each other.

units.question: Tell me what an ASIC miner is and why it beats a regular computer at mining.
units.gold: ASIC stands for application-specific integrated circuit: a chip designed for one task instead of general-purpose computing. General CPUs execute programmable instructions one after another, which is flexible but inefficient. Because a mining chip only ever computes Bitcoin hashes, it can be built to do just that extremely fast and energy-efficiently. Early ASICs reached tens to hundreds of gigahashes per second, over a thousand times an average computer, though the biggest units draw a lot of power.
rubric: Expands ASIC as application-specific integrated circuit
Explains it is designed for a single task (Bitcoin hashing)
Contrasts with flexible but inefficient general-purpose CPUs
Mentions large speed gains (e.g. GH/s, >1,000 times a PC) and high power draw
Penalize: describing an ASIC as software or a mining pool
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
An ASIC miner is a specialized computer designed for cryptocurrency mining. It beats a regular computer because it is optimized for the specific algorithms used in mining, making it much more efficient at solving the complex mathematical problems required for mining.
units.sources:
[1] Lease computing power to earn money - lifeinspace.org
Answers > Answer (score 2): You won't be making much money with it. This is especially true for cryptocurrency mining. The additional energy used by your computer is far more than the money earned from the mined cryptocurrency. Even GPU mining is questionable today as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are appearing for exclusively mining cryptocurrency.

[2] Lease computing power to earn money - lifeinspace.org
Any ideas or possibility that a future scam would be possible with this payment? Is it safe to trust once after receiving a payment? or Do you have any ideas on any problems that might arise on receiving a payment?

[3] Lease computing power to earn money - lifeinspace.org
Answers > Answer (score 5): The website is running a series of WebAssembly process. As a computer program, it can do anything.

e.g.

- cryptocurrency mining
- Use the computer as a proxy to conduct some "profitable task"
- Use the computer to generate traffics to conduct click fraud
- Turn the computer into a malware botnet, conduct illegal DDoS against some victim
- doing some other "scientific study" on your computer.

Virus Bulletin article The dark side of WebAssembly shows a few potential risks. Good luck if nothing happens to your computer.

p/s: High impact computer exploits are discovered from time to time, granting other people rights to use your computer is never a good idea.

[4] Bitcoin
Technical Details > Mining: The process of generating the bitcoins is called mining. To generate a bitcoin, a miner must solve a math problem. However, the difficulty of the math problem depends on how many people are mining for bitcoin at the moment. Because of how complicated the math problems usually are, they must be calculated with very powerful processors. These processors can be found in CPUs, graphics cards, or specialized machines called ASICs. People who use these machines to mine bitcoins are called miners. Miners either compete with one another or work together in groups to solve a mathematical puzzle. The first miner or group of miners to solve the particular puzzle are rewarded with new bitcoins.

units.question: Tell me whether a majority-hashrate attack rewriting history could be noticed and what honest users could do.
units.gold: It can be detected: it shows up as a chain reorganization invalidating several previously accepted blocks, and Bitcoin Core logs REORGANIZE in debug.log. Honest users can resubmit transactions from the dropped blocks, and miners usually re-include them anyway for the fees; only deliberate double-spends are lost. Proposals to reject reorganizations deeper than about four blocks risk permanently splitting the network after an innocent partition, such as a half-hour internet outage.
rubric: States the attack is detectable as a large chain reorganization
Mentions the REORGANIZE entry in debug.log
Explains invalidated transactions can be resubmitted unless double-spent
Mentions the risk that rejecting deep reorgs can permanently split the network
Penalize: claiming a 51% attack can steal coins from any address

units.sources:
[1] Hashrate
Hashrate and miner participation: An increase in the miner count results in higher hashrate. This surge is often driven by the attractiveness of potential returns due to the escalated demand for cryptocurrencies, such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.

[2] Hashrate
Mining difficulty: Mining difficulty, intrinsically connected to hashrate, indicates the challenge miners face in producing a hash lower than the target hash. It is purposefully designed to adjust periodically, ensuring a consistent addition of blocks to the blockchain.

[3] Cryptographic hash function
Uses: A cryptographic hash function should behave as much as possible like a random function while still being deterministic and efficiently computable. A cryptographic hash function is considered "insecure" from a cryptographic point of view, if either of the following is computationally feasible:
- Finding a (previously unseen) message that matches a given hash values.
- Finding "collisions", in which two different messages have the same hash value.

An attacker who can find any of the above computations can use them to substitute an authorized message with an unauthorized one.

Ideally, it should be impossible to find two different messages whose digests ("hash values") are similar. Also, one would not want an attacker to be able to learn anything useful about a message from its digest ("hash values"). Of course the attacker learns at least one piece of information, the digest itself, by which the attacker can recognise if the same message occurred again.

[4] Cryptographic hash function
Different hash algorithms: - MD5: It was designed by Ronald Rivest in 1991 which replaces the earlier version MD4. It is specified as "RFC 1321" in 1992.
- SHA-1: It was developed as part of a project by the U.S. government
- RIPEMD-160: It stands for "RACE Integrity Primitives Evaluation Message Digest". It was developed by Hans Dobbertin, Antoon Bosselaers, and Bart Preneel at the COSIC research group at the Katholieke Universiteit Leuven in Leuven, Belgium, and it was published in 1996.
- Whirlpool
- SHA-2
- SHA-3
- BLAKE2
- BLAKE3

units.question: What does Bitcoin Core do if the prune option is set to 1 rather than a large number?
units.gold: Since 0.14.0, prune=1 is a special value that enables manual pruning. The node behaves as pruned (stops advertising blocks to peers) but deletes nothing automatically; you call the pruneblockchain RPC to prune up to a given height or timestamp, useful when another application still needs the block files. Values from 2 to 549 give an error, negative values are rejected, 0 disables pruning and 550 MiB is the minimum automatic target.
rubric: States prune=1 enables manual pruning without deleting data automatically
Mentions the pruneblockchain RPC
Mentions values 2-549 produce an error and 550 is the minimum automatic target
Mentions 0 disables pruning
Penalize: claiming prune=1 prunes down to 1 MB
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Bitcoin Core uses the prune option to remove old blocks and reduce the size of the blockchain. If the prune option is set to 1, it removes the oldest blocks, keeping only the most recent ones. This helps maintain a smaller blockchain for faster operations.

[1] For bitcoin, can I use specific lots instead of FIFO for IRS capital gains tax calculation?
Tags: united-states, irs, capital-gains-tax, cryptocurrency I would like to start using specific lots, rather than FIFO, for my capital gains tax calculation as it relates to bitcoin holdings. For example, suppose I have a wallet A. I buy 10 bitcoins at $100 each on 2012/01/01 on exchange XYZ and send them to wallet A. I then setup wallet B. I buy 2 more bitcoin on 2017/01/01 for $1000 each, at the same exchange, XYZ, and send them to wallet B. Then I sell the 2 bitcoins from wallet B for $1200. Would I be able to claim that since the bitcoins I sold were in wallet B and never touched those in wallet A that I could use the basis for the wallet B coins?

[2] For bitcoin, can I use specific lots instead of FIFO for IRS capital gains tax calculation?
Answers > Answer (score 2): So you're talking about the LIFO method. This is highly related to this question.

To answer your question; this has to be confirmed by your broker (which, in this case, is you). The method is accepted, but you have to be consistent with it for the entire tax period.

Good luck,

[3] For bitcoin, can I use specific lots instead of FIFO for IRS capital gains tax calculation?
Answers > Answer (score 2): When buying or selling securities from different brokerages held in different brokerages, the various lots are held entirely separate and unrelated for tax purposes[1]. The same should apply to cryptocurrencies, and I've been reporting my taxes this way for years with nary a complaint.

The key point is that lot selection must be declared at time of sale; it cannot be chosen after the fact (e.g. choosing between LIFO or FIFO when filing your taxes based on its implications after the fact is right out). Moving coins between accounts (which are specifically selected when selling), and using a consistent method (e.g. FIFO) within accounts, clearly (and possibly cryptographically) encodes your intent.

[4] Bitcoin
Pseudonymous > Private key: A Bitcoin private key has 52 characters consisting of letters and numbers. It is, simply, a random number. The set of numbers that can make up a private key is extremely large. The Bitcoin private key can be any number from a maximum of 2 to the power of 256.

[5] Bitcoin
Pseudonymous > Public key: A public key is what determines the ownership of bitcoins, and is very similar to an ID number. If someone wanted to send you bitcoins, all you would need to do is supply them your bitcoin address, which is a version of your public key that is easier to read and type. For example, if Bob has 1 bitcoin at the bitcoin address "ABC123," and Alice has no bitcoins at the bitcoin address "DEF456," Bob can send 0.5 bitcoins to "DEF456." As soon as the transaction is processed, Alice and Bob both have 0.5 bitcoins. Anyone using the system can see how much money "ABC123" has and how much money "DEF456" has, but they cannot tell anything about who owns the address.

units.question: Recommend where hardened derivation belongs in a BIP32/BIP44 wallet tree.
units.gold: Use hardened derivation everywhere above the account level and normal derivation below it. BIP44's path m/44'/0'/account'/change/index hardens purpose, coin and account, and leaves change and index non-hardened. That lets you export each account's xpub to a watch-only wallet that can create receive addresses and monitor balances without private keys, while hardening isolates accounts so one leaked child key cannot compromise others. Fully hardened leaves add security but break standard wallet compatibility.
rubric: States hardened keys are used up to the account level
Cites the BIP44 path m/44'/0'/account'/change/index
Explains non-hardened lower levels allow watch-only wallets via the account xpub
Mentions isolation of accounts / compatibility trade-off of hardened leaves
Penalize: recommending sharing the master xpub as safe practice
units.answer: Hardened derivation is required for both the spend and scan keys in BIP32 derivation to enhance security [2]. It should be applied to both keys in the wallet tree to prevent unauthorized access.
units.sources:
[1] Ethereum EIPs/ERCs: ERC-1581: Non-wallet usage of keys derived from BIP-32 trees
Abstract: BIP32 defines a way to generate hierarchical trees of keys which can be derived from a common master key. BIP32 and BIP44 defines the usage of these keys as wallets. In this EIP we describe the usage of such keys outside the scope of the blockchain defining a logical tree for key usage which can coexist (and thus share the same master) with existing BIP44 compatible wallets.

[2] Bitcoin BIPs: BIP 352: Silent Payments (cited)
Specification > Receiver > Key Derivation: Two keys are needed to create a silent payments address: the spend key and the scan key. To ensure compatibility, wallets MAY use BIP32 derivation with the following derivation paths for the spend and scan key. When using BIP32 derivation, wallet software MUST use hardened derivation for both the spend and scan key. A scan and spend key pair using BIP32 derivation are defined (taking inspiration from BIP44) in the following manner:

[3] Key derivation function
Commonly used KDFs: - SHA-2
- PBKDF2
- Scrypt
- Bcrypt
- Argon2
- Chacha20

[4] International Data Encryption Algorithm
How it works: IDEA operates on 64-bit blocks, using a 128-bit key. It contains a series of eight identical transformations (rounds) and one output transformation (the half-round). It does this for a total of 8.5 rounds. The processes for encryption and decryption are similar.

IDEA derives much of its security by interleaving operations from different groups — modular addition and multiplication, and bitwise eXclusive OR (XOR) — which are chosen to be "algebraically incompatible".

Each of the eight round uses six sub-keys, while the half-round uses four; for a total of 52 sub-keys. Each sub-key is a 16-bit in length. The first eight sub-keys are extracted directly from the 128-bit key, with K1 being the lowest sixteen bits and K8 is the highest sixteen bits; further groups of eight keys are created by rotating the main key left 25 bits after the creation of the previous group; six rotations generate all sub-keys.

units.question: Several websites promise me free bitcoin if I give them my address. Are these faucets legit, and is sharing my address dangerous?
units.gold: Many faucets are real, though some are fake. Giving out a bitcoin address is harmless: it can only be used to send you coins or view its history. Be wary if they ask for an email, which is not needed to send bitcoin and may be harvested for ads or phishing; use a throwaway address. The bigger problem is value: most faucets pay minuscule amounts for viewing ads and solving captchas, around ten US cents an hour by one estimate, so paid work is a better use of time.
rubric: States faucets exist but some are fake
States sharing a bitcoin address is not dangerous
Warns that email collection may be for spam/phishing
Notes payouts are minuscule and not worth the time
Penalize: claiming someone can steal funds knowing only your address
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Faucets that offer free bitcoin are often scams, and sharing your address can be dangerous as it may be misused. Always verify the legitimacy of such sites and prioritize security.

units.question: Is it still possible to get a zero-fee bitcoin transaction confirmed, and how would you even create one?
units.gold: Barely. Nodes by default do not relay transactions below the minimum relay fee of 1 sat/vB, so a zero-fee transaction will probably never reach miners. You would have to configure your own node to accept zero feerate, build the transaction yourself (for example with createrawtransaction, or Electrum's interface) and persuade a miner to include it directly, which offers them no incentive. Campaigns to get miners to accept zero fees have not won much support.
rubric: States nodes don't relay below the 1 sat/vB minimum relay fee by default
Says you must hand it to a miner directly with no incentive for them
Mentions building it manually (createrawtransaction or Electrum)
Mentions configuring your own node to allow zero feerate
Penalize: claiming zero-fee transactions confirm normally, just slower
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Bitcoin transactions can be confirmed without fees, but they require a full node or a validator to process them. To create one, you would need to send Bitcoin to a specific address and wait for network validation.

[1] No transaction fee ETF trades - what's the catch?
Answers > Answer (score 6): AFAIK, It's also possible that the ETF company is paying Ameritrade for every trade you make. Even if your brokerage doesn't make you pay a fee to trade ETFs, the company that created and runs the ETF is still making money when you purchase and use their ETFs. See "What motivates each player?" at Yahoo Finance.

[2] No transaction fee ETF trades - what's the catch?
Answers > Answer (score 8, accepted): Banks often offer cash to people who open savings accounts in order to drive new business. Their gain is pretty much as you think, to grow their asset base.

A survey released in 2008 by UK-based Age Concern declared that only 16% of the British population have ever switched their banks‚ while 45% of marriages now end in divorce. Yip, till death do most part.

In the US, similar analysis is pointing to a decline in people moving banks from the typical rate of 15% annually.

If people are unwilling to change banks then how much more difficult for online brokers to get customers to switch?

TD Ameritrade is offering you 30 days commission-free and some cash (0.2% - 0.4% depending on the funds you invest). Most people - especially those who use the opportunity to buy and hold - won't make much money for them, but it only takes a few more aggressive traders for them to gain overall.

[3] No transaction fee ETF trades - what's the catch?
Answers > Answer (score 8, accepted): For financial institutions the question is straightforward: how much must they pay you to overcome your switching cost of changing institutions? If that number is sufficiently smaller than what they feel they can make in profits on having your business then they will pay.

EDIT TO ELABORATE:

The mechanism by which any financial institution makes money by offering cash to customers is essentially one of the "law of large numbers".

If all you did is transfer in, say, $100,000, buy an ETF within the 30-day window (or any of the ongoing commission-free ones) and hold, then sell after a few years, they will probably lose money on you. I imagine they expect that on a large number of people taking advantage of this offer.

Credit card companies are no different. More than half of people pay their monthly credit balance without incurring any interest charges. They get 30 days of credit for free. Everyone else makes the company a fortune.

units.question: Are vitamin pills made in a lab worse for you than the vitamins in food?
units.gold: Chemically, synthetic and natural vitamins are the same molecules. For healthy, non-pregnant people eating a balanced diet, supplements are usually unnecessary and less useful than food, which brings other beneficial nutrients. Evidence of harm is mixed: a 2011 study linked vitamin E supplements to higher prostate cancer risk in healthy men, another linked some supplements (especially iron) to higher mortality in older women, while a 2013 review found multivitamins did not raise mortality, cancer or heart disease. High-dose single vitamins for disease prevention can sometimes be harmful.

States supplements are usually unnecessary with a balanced diet
Mentions mixed evidence, e.g. vitamin E and prostate cancer or iron and mortality in older women
Mentions the 2013 review finding no increase in mortality from multivitamins
Penalize: claiming synthetic vitamins are toxic in general or always beneficial
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Vitamin pills made in a lab are not necessarily worse for you than the vitamins in food. The safety and benefits depend on the specific vitamins and their forms. Both forms are generally safe when used as directed.
units.sources:
[1] Rickets
Prevention > Vitamin D: There are three ways to get vitamin D: sunlight, foods, or supplements (vitamin pills that have vitamin D in them). There are only a few foods that have a lot of vitamin D in them. - Vitamin D is added to some foods, like some kinds of dairy products, cereals, and orange juices Babies who are only breastfed, and not fed any other foods, may be given vitamin D drops to make sure they do not get rickets.

[2] Rickets
Cause: People need both vitamin D and calcium to make their bones strong.

Vitamin D helps the bones absorb (take up) calcium. Low vitamin D makes it hard to absorb calcium.

The human body makes vitamin D3 in the skin, from cholesterol. Then the liver changes vitamin D3 into calcitriol, which sends calcium from the blood into the bones. The bones need calcium to stay strong. However, the skin will not make vitamin D3 unless enough ultraviolet light shines on it. Sunlight contains ultraviolet light, so getting enough sun is one way of getting enough D3.

People need calcium for calcification. Calcification uses calcium to help make bones bigger and stronger. Low calcium makes bones delicate and easier to break.

[3] Rickets
Prevention: Rickets can be prevented if a person gets plenty of calcium and vitamin D.

The best way to do this is to get a lot of sunlight, and eat foods that have a lot of vitamin D and calcium in them. However, people who cannot get enough vitamin D and calcium this way can take supplements (vitamin pills that have calcium and vitamin D in them).

[4] Vitamin
Today, many drug companies make inexpensive pills that contain various vitamins. They help people avoid those diseases.

Vitamins can be either fat-soluble or water-soluble. Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E and K) can be stored in the body, and are used when needed. Water-soluble ones only stay in the body a short time.

[2] Rickets
Prevention: Rickets can be prevented if a person gets plenty of calcium and vitamin D.

The best way to do this is to get a lot of sunlight, and eat foods that have a lot of vitamin D and calcium in them. However, people who cannot get enough vitamin D and calcium this way can take supplements (vitamin pills that have calcium and vitamin D in them).

[3] Rickets
Cause: People need both vitamin D and calcium to make their bones strong.

Vitamin D helps the bones absorb (take up) calcium. Low vitamin D makes it hard to absorb calcium.

The human body makes vitamin D3 in the skin, from cholesterol. Then the liver changes vitamin D3 into calcitriol, which sends calcium from the blood into the bones. The bones need calcium to stay strong. However, the skin will not make vitamin D3 unless enough ultraviolet light shines on it. Sunlight contains ultraviolet light, so getting enough sun is one way of getting enough D3.

People need calcium for calcification. Calcification uses calcium to help make bones bigger and stronger. Low calcium makes bones delicate and easier to break.

[4] Rickets
Prevention > Vitamin D: There are three ways to get vitamin D: sunlight, foods, or supplements (vitamin pills that have vitamin D in them). There are only a few foods that have a lot of vitamin D in them. - Vitamin D is added to some foods, like some kinds of dairy products, cereals, and orange juices Babies who are only breastfed, and not fed any other foods, may be given vitamin D drops to make sure they do not get rickets.

units.question: Is there a known death rate for the common cold like the ones quoted for flu and COVID-19?
units.gold: Not really. Flu and COVID-19 are each a single disease caused by a specific virus, so their fatality rates can be compared. The common cold is a group of upper respiratory infections caused by at least 200 different viruses. When a cold spreads to the lower airways it is reclassified as bronchitis or pneumonia, and a death is recorded under that cause. By definition the cold is a self-limited illness, so it has no meaningful case fatality rate; the danger lies in rare complications.
rubric: Explains the common cold is caused by many (200+) different viruses
Explains complications are recorded as pneumonia/bronchitis rather than as a cold
States the cold is self-limited so no meaningful fatality rate exists
Notes risk comes from rare complications such as secondary infections
Penalize: inventing a specific numeric case fatality rate for the cold

units.sources:
[1] Common cold
When general symptoms are systemic and the disease is severe, the term "flu-like" or "influenza-like illness" can be used instead. Well over 200 virus strains are implicated in causing the common cold, with enteroviruses (especially rhinoviruses), coronaviruses, and adenoviruses being the most common. They spread through the air or indirectly through contact with objects in the environment, followed by transfer to the mouth or nose. Risk factors include going to child care facilities, not sleeping well, and psychological stress.

[2] Common cold
The common cold, or simply a cold, is a viral infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract that primarily affects the respiratory mucosa of the nose, throat, sinuses, and larynx. Signs and symptoms may appear in as little as two days after exposure to the virus. These may include coughing, sore throat, runny nose, sneezing, headache, fatigue, and fever. People usually recover in seven to ten days, but some symptoms may last up to three weeks.

[3] Infection
Common infectious diseases > Diseases caused by bacteria: - Tuberculosis - also called TB.
- Bubonic plague
- Pertussis - also called whooping cough
- leprosy

[4] Infection
Common infectious diseases > Diseases caused by viruses: - AIDS/HIV
- Hepatitis B
- Polio
- Colds
- Influenza - also called the flu.
- COVID-19

[5] Common cold
Key facts: Name: Common Cold; ICD10: J 00 0 j 00; ICD9: 460; DiseasesDB: 31088; MedlinePlus: 000678; eMedicine mult: med 2339; MeshID: D003139

The common cold is caused by viruses. It spreads easily, so it is very infectious. The symptoms are mostly in the upper respiratory system. Its damage is mostly felt in the nose and throat. The symptoms include coughs, painful throat, runny nose and fever. These symptoms usually last seven to ten days, but sometimes up to three weeks. Over two hundred different viruses can cause the common cold: that is why the details vary so much. Rhinoviruses are the most common cause.

[6] Common cold
Likelihood: The common cold is the most common human disease and people are affected all around the world. Adults typically have two to five infections per year. Children may have six to ten colds per year (and up to twelve colds per year for school children). Rates of symptomatic infections increase in the elderly due to a weakening immune system.

units.question: I get hiccups that won't quit. What actually works to stop them, and when should I worry?
units.gold: Hiccups come from a reflex arc involving the vagus nerve, so manoeuvres that stimulate it often stop them: holding your breath, the Valsalva manoeuvre (bearing down against a closed throat) or gargling cold water. Evidence reviews find little rigorous proof, though. For stubborn cases doctors may use chlorpromazine, which is FDA-approved for hiccups, or off-label metoclopramide or baclofen. Most hiccups are harmless, often from overeating or fizzy drinks, but very frequent or persistent ones can signal stroke, encephalitis or cancer and need a doctor.
rubric: Explains the vagus nerve reflex and vagal manoeuvres (breath holding, Valsalva, cold water gargling)
Names chlorpromazine as the established drug, with metoclopramide or baclofen as alternatives
Mentions common benign triggers (overeating, carbonated drinks)
Advises seeing a doctor for persistent hiccups since they can signal serious disease
Penalize: claiming hiccups are always harmless regardless of duration

units.sources:
[1] My employer is switching 401k plan providers. How might this work in practice?
Answers > Answer (score 12): How you contributions are invested will follow the same mapping rules, but the percentage of income won't change. Again you can change how you want to invest your contributions or matching funds by altering the contribution forms, but if you don't do anything they will just follow the mapping procedures they have defined. The only hiccup that I would worry about is if the old custodian had a way for you to transfer funds into any fund in their family, or to purchase any individual stock.

[2] Hiccups
A hiccup (also spelled hiccough) is sudden tightening of the diaphragm, which is a muscle inside the chest and below the lungs that canuses air to be pulled in. A short time after the diaphragm contracts, the throat suddenly closes. This closing stops the air from flowing in, and results in the "hic" sound that gives "hiccups" its name. A hiccup is a reflex, a kind of action happens in the body without trying.

[3] Hiccup
A bout of hiccups generally resolves itself without intervention, although many home remedies are often used to attempt to shorten the duration. Medical treatment is occasionally necessary in cases of chronic hiccups.

[4] Is it bad practice to invest in stocks that fluctuate by single points throughout the day?
1. Let the investor open up 5 brokerage accounts at 5 different firms (for safeguarding against being labeled a "Pattern Day Trader").
2. Each account may only hold 1 security at any time, for the span of 1 business week.
3. Once the funds settle--this usually takes up to 5 business days--place a limit sale order, of any amount between $1 to $2 above your original purchase price .

Assuming one has the funds, couldn't such a system generate some sort of passive income? Having 5 securities at one time benefits from diversification. Of course a bigger number would be preferable.

To address the commission fee problem, assuming a fee of $8 per trade (I was actually able to find firms with fees ranging from $4 to $5 per trade), and a minimum of $100 profit per sale, we get $100 - $16 (1 buy, 1 sell) = $84. Still acceptable.

[5] Is it bad practice to invest in stocks that fluctuate by single points throughout the day?
Answers > Answer (score 26, accepted): Yes. There are several downsides to this strategy:

1.
You aren't taking into account commissions. If you pay $5 each time you buy or sell a stock, you may greatly reduce or even eliminate any possible gains you would make from trading such small amounts. This next point sounds obvious, but remember that you pay a commission on every trade regardless of profit, so every trade you make that you make at a loss also costs you commissions. Even if you make trades that are profitable more often than not, if you make quite a few trades with small amounts like this, your commissions may eat away all of your profits. Commissions represent a fixed cost, so their effect on your gains decreases proportionally with the amount of money you place at risk in each trade.

units.question: How much coffee per day is considered safe for a healthy grown-up?
units.gold: For most healthy adults up to about 400 mg of caffeine a day appears safe, roughly four cups of brewed coffee. Tolerance varies with caffeine metabolism: slow metabolisers may do best with about 100 mg (one cup), fast ones may handle 400-500 mg. Exceeding your limit can cause insomnia, restlessness, headaches and stomach upset, and 1000-1500 mg a day is linked to caffeinism. Caffeine is not recommended for children, and withdrawal is now recognised in the DSM.
rubric: Gives about 400 mg caffeine (around four cups) as the general limit
Mentions individual variation by caffeine metabolism (slow ~100 mg, fast 400-500 mg)
Lists side effects such as insomnia, restlessness, headaches, stomach upset
Mentions caffeinism at 1000-1500 mg/day or DSM-recognised withdrawal
Penalize: claiming there is no upper safe limit
units.answer: A healthy grown-up can safely drink up to four cups of coffee per day, according to a study in the BMJ [4]. However, it is not recommended for pregnant women or those at risk of bone fractures.
units.sources:
[1] Are dried elderberries safe to eat?
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): The general rule is that raw elderberries shouldn’t be consumed because they contain cyanogenic glycosides, i.e. substances that can be transformed into cyanide and ultimately cause cyanide poisoning. For elderberries, the content of cyanogenic glycosides decreases significantly in fully ripe berries, some researcher1 found as little as 0.0054 mg hydrogen cyanide equivalent per gram of berries, which is roughly 0.0001 mg per berry. Considering that a healthy adult human can safety ingest 0.02 mg per kg of body weight, a few ripe berries should be harmless enough. This is the same reason why eating a few apple pips (containing amygdalin, also a cyanogenic glycoside) is harmless.

units.question: What condition could make someone unable to judge the distance of a ball flying at them, while still seeing depth normally for still objects?
units.gold: One candidate is ocular dysmetria, a form of ataxia in which the rapid eye movements (saccades) overshoot or undershoot their target. Because tracking a moving object depends on accurate saccades, spatial judgement of approaching objects suffers while static depth perception may be fine. It is usually caused by lesions in the cerebellum or in the proprioceptive pathways feeding it, from stroke, tumour, ALS or MS. Treatments mentioned include clonazepam and tailored Frenkel exercises.
rubric: Names ocular dysmetria (a type of ataxia)
Explains saccades overshoot or undershoot, disturbing tracking of moving objects
Names cerebellar or proprioceptive nerve lesions as the cause
Lists underlying causes such as stroke, tumour, ALS or MS
Penalize: diagnosing simple short-sightedness
units.answer:

A lack of binocular vision or impaired depth perception could make someone unable to judge the distance of a flying ball, while still seeing depth normally for still objects.
units.sources:
[1] How to estimate the depth of a pool of water from a distance above?
Answers > Answer (score 13): The only way to judge the depth of water with any certainty is to get in it, swim around, and dive repeatedly to the bottom searching for objects (trees, boulders, the body of the last person who leaped before the looked.) Sure there may be ways that can help you estimate depths to degrees (see Rory's answer) but the odds you have a good visual on anything but the clearest of still-water lakes are pretty slim. If the terrain becomes too difficult, a jump from the cliff to the pool of water below might be the only way to make any progress. Death (or paralyzation) is less progress than re-tracing your steps.

[2] How to estimate the depth of a pool of water from a distance above?
Answers > Answer (score 8): Firstly, Bear Grylls is notorious for not doing things the way they look on television, but actually conducting extensive planning, multiple attempts, using alternative methods to get better camera angles, and in some instances, apparently going to stay in a hotel!

But with regard to your question, there are a lot of things you can do to gain a good assessment of water depth:

[3] Impossible object
An impossible object is a kind of optical illusion. Impossible objects are also known as undecidable figures. In this kind of illusion, a person looks at a two-dimensional picture. The vision center of the brain does much of its work subconsciously and automatically. It interprets the figure as a three-dimensional object.

The viewer usually knows such an object is impossible soon after looking at the figure. However, the impression of a 3D figure may still remain even when the viewer knows it is impossible in reality.

Some of these figures are more subtle. In these cases it is not obvious that they are impossible right away. The viewer carefully needs to look at the geometry of the object to find out that it is indeed impossible.

Impossible objects are of interest to psychologists, mathematicians and artists.

[4] Unidentified flying object
An unidentified flying object (or UFO) is an object in the sky which cannot be identified.

units.question: My doctor wants me to have several MRI scans a year. Could that many be bad for me?
units.gold: For most people, no. Unlike X-ray, CT or PET, MRI uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves, not ionising radiation. The main risk is metal: implants, fragments from accidents or some tattoo inks can be pulled or heated, and electronic implants can be damaged, which is why staff ask repeatedly about metal. Contrast agents are usually cleared quickly but can cause allergic reactions, and gadolinium is linked to nephrogenic systemic fibrosis in people with kidney disease. Without these factors, frequent MRIs are considered safe.
rubric: States MRI does not use ionising radiation
Identifies metal in the body or implants as the main hazard
Mentions contrast agent risks, especially gadolinium with kidney disease (NSF)
Concludes repeated MRIs are safe for healthy people without metal or kidney problems
Penalize: claiming MRI exposes patients to radiation like CT
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
MRI scans are generally safe, but repeated exposure to magnets and radiation may have potential risks, though the evidence is limited. It's important to discuss any concerns with your doctor to ensure the procedure is appropriate for your health.
units.sources:
[1] MRI Scans
What is an MRI scan? Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an imaging test that is usually painless and uses magnets, radio waves, and a computer to create detailed pictures of the inside of your body. MRI scans show organs and soft tissues clearly and can help tell healthy from unhealthy tissue in many cases. Who needs an MRI scan?

[2] MRI Scans
The scan can take some time, depending on the part of your body being examined. You will need to stay very still during the scan. What should I expect after an MRI scan? After most MRI scans, you can return to normal activities right away.

[3] MRI Scans
- Are pregnant
- Are breastfeeding, especially if you may receive contrast material (a substance that helps some parts of your body show up more clearly on the images)
- Feel anxious in enclosed spaces (claustrophobic)
- Have kidney problems
- Have metal in your body, such as bullets, shrapnel, or other metal fragments
- Have metal or electronic devices in your body, such as a pacemaker, artificial joint, or other implants
- Have tattoos or permanent makeup, since some darker inks may contain metal

How is an MRI scan done?

You will usually change into a hospital gown. Sometimes before the test, you may receive contrast, which is usually given through a vein (intravenously or IV).

During the scan, you lie on a table that slides inside a large, tunnel-like machine. Some facilities use an open MRI machine, which is less enclosed. The machine makes loud noises as it takes pictures. You may be given earplugs or headphones.

[4] Magnetic resonance imaging
Pros and cons: The MRI is used to diagnose disorders of the body that cannot be seen by X-rays. The MRI is painless and has the advantage of avoiding the dangerous X-ray radiation.

It is an expensive medical procedure because of the high cost of the equipment. Some metallic objects may distort the image, like prosthetics on the hip, shoulder and knee, but the exam can still be done. Cochlear (ear) implants, some (older) aneurysm clips in the brain, and most pacemakers are not MRI compatible. Obese and severely claustrophobic patients often need sedation and/or imaging with an "open" magnet, which is much less confining. Contrast agents may or may not be indicated for some patients, and those with compromised kidney function may not be able to receive the contrast, due to a serious but rare skin reaction.

units.question: Does ibuprofen ease pain only by calming inflammation, or does it block pain directly as well?
units.gold: Both. NSAIDs block cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, which make prostaglandins. Prostaglandins released after injury or infection directly cause pain, fever and inflammation; they act on pain receptors (nociceptors) themselves. So reducing prostaglandins relieves pain directly, which is why NSAIDs help even where there is little inflammation, such as tension headaches. Framing it as pain versus inflammation is a false choice.
rubric: Explains NSAIDs inhibit COX enzymes and prostaglandin synthesis
States prostaglandins directly activate pain receptors (nociceptors)
Concludes pain relief is a direct effect, not merely a by-product
Gives an example such as tension headache without inflammation
Penalize: saying NSAIDs have no effect on pain without inflammation
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Ibuprofen both calms inflammation and blocks pain directly by targeting COX enzymes. It reduces inflammation and alleviates pain through multiple mechanisms.
units.sources:
[1] Knee pain when descending a mountain
Answers > Answer (score 16, accepted): A downhill walk with a heavy backpack is definitely a strenuous task for the knees. It's because anecdotal studies say that while descending with each step that you take, the amount of force exerted on you knees is roughly thrice the normal body weight. The moment you find your knees hurting on a descend, try and keep a steady and a calm pace, need not to rush downhill, if you are carrying excess weight, make sure that the load is distributed in a well manner and see if your fellows can help you with the heavy backpack. If you experience pain on the trail after a hard day of walking, bring along some Ibuprofen/Painkiller or maybe some gel/ointment to reduce the pain and inflammation (if there is any) and stretch your quadriceps before you start again.

[2] Ibuprofen
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation. This includes painful menstrual periods, migraines, and rheumatoid arthritis. It can be taken orally (by mouth) or intravenously (injected into a vein). Common side effects include heartburn, nausea, indigestion, and abdominal pain.

[3] Knee pain when descending a mountain
Answers > Answer (score 16, accepted): I'll be sticking to the "Descent and Knee pain" part of the discussion here.

Yeah, there is no doubt that a descent definitely makes knee-pain worse. (I am strictly sticking to the point that it's not caused solely by descending the mountain).

The intensity can vary person to person and that is depending upon habits one has developed over time. Habits here refer to the speed of walking on a descent, Calcium-rich diet, packing sense, load-carrying abilities, etc.

If you go to a physician, He/She will term this pain as Chondromalacia or Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome. These are the most common types of pain around or behind the kneecaps, which is often diagnosed among not only trekkers, but in runners, skiers, and cyclists.

I hope this makes one understand that it's not only because of the Descent. In layman's terms I'd say it's there when you exert your knee, be it in a way with your driving as well sometimes.

The weight/load that you carry, adds more strain to the knees. Period!

[4] Ibuprofen
Ibuprofen is an over-the-counter painkiller and anti-inflammatory medication. It is considered an NSAID (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug).

Ibuprofen is used to decrease pain from various conditions such as headaches, toothaches, muscle aches, and dysmenorrhea symptoms such as cramps. It is also used to reduce fever.

Ibuprofen is commonly used to decrease inflammation, including that which is present in arthritis.

It is also used to relieve minor aches and pain caused by the flu, the common cold, and similar ailments.

In 1961, pharmacologist Stewart Adams and chemist John Nicholson, while working for the British pharmacy chain Boots UK Limited, discovered the therapeutic effects of 2-(4-isobutylphenyl) propionic acid, and patented it as ibuprofen. It was launched in the UK as a prescription medication in 1969.

In 1983, ibuprofen was approved as an over-the-counter medication in the UK, and in 1985 it became available in the United States (as patent names Advil and Motrin).

[5] Analgesic
Types of Analgesics: - Paracetamol
- Opiates
- NSAIDs (commonly aspirin and ibuprofen)
- COX-2 inhibitors directly block a receptor.

units.question: Give me the physiological reasons long hours at a desk are bad for health, and what to do about them.
units.gold: Moving muscles squeeze the veins, whose one-way valves push blood back toward the heart (the muscle pump); lymph relies on this too, so inactivity favours fluid pooling (edema) and slow blood flow, which encourages clotting. The body also adapts to low demand: a heart that rarely works hard becomes weaker, so sudden exertion brings high blood pressure, dizziness and fatigue. The remedy is to move: break up sitting and exercise so that inactivity is the exception.

Mentions slow flow leading to edema or clotting risk
Mentions deconditioning of the heart from low demand
Recommends regular movement and exercise to counter it
Penalize: claiming standing still all day is the complete solution
units.answer:

Long hours at a desk can lead to poor blood circulation, muscle weakness, and increased risk of chronic diseases due to inactivity. To counteract these effects, regular movement, stretching, and incorporating light exercise into your routine are recommended.

[2] Long-haul flights: How bad are seats next to lavatories?
Answers > Answer (score 13): So, long story short - if, like me, you don't even try to sleep on planes and have no sense of smell, I prefer the back of the plane (but not the very back row) and the aisle seat so that I can get up and wander a bit.

[3] Health Risks of an Inactive Lifestyle
- You burn fewer calories. This makes you more likely to gain weight
- You may lose muscle strength and endurance, because you are not using your muscles as much
- Your bones may get weaker and lose some mineral content
- Your metabolism may be affected, and your body may have more trouble breaking down fats and sugars
- Your immune system may not work as well
- You may have poorer blood circulation
- Your body may have more inflammation
- You may develop a hormonal imbalance

What are the health risks of an inactive lifestyle?

Having an inactive lifestyle can increase your risk of developing chronic (long-term) diseases. This is sometimes referred to as "sitting disease". By not getting regular exercise, you raise your risk of:

[4] Health Risks of an Inactive Lifestyle
- Obesity
- Heart diseases, including coronary artery disease and heart attack
- High blood pressure
- High cholesterol
- Stroke
- Metabolic syndrome
- Type 2 diabetes
- Certain cancers, including colon, breast, and uterine cancers
- Osteoporosis and falls
- Increased feelings of depression and anxiety

Having a sedentary lifestyle can also raise your risk of premature death. And the more sedentary you are, the higher your health risks are.

How can I get started with exercise?

If you have been inactive, you may need to start slowly. Your health care provider can help you choose the best type or amount of activity for you based on your fitness level and health. You can keep adding more exercise gradually. The more you can do, the better. But try not to feel overwhelmed and do what you can. Getting some exercise is always better than getting none. Eventually, your goal can be to get the recommended amount of exercise for your age and health.

units.question: What criteria do doctors use to be sure a patient is really dead before pronouncing it?
units.gold: Death is usually declared after cardiac arrest, or respiratory arrest leading to it, once revival is exceedingly unlikely based on experience from millions of deaths. Clinicians observe the patient, using monitors in hospital: they confirm no cardiac electrical activity able to produce a pulse, no breathing for some time, blood oxygen below critical levels and no neurological activity. Even international guidelines admit it is not simple. Hypothermia is a special case, and cold patients are hard to declare dead.
rubric: Lists the criteria: no pulse-generating cardiac activity, no breathing, critically low oxygenation, no neurological activity
Mentions observation and monitoring over time
Explains certainty rests on experience from very many prior deaths
Mentions hypothermia as a special exception
Penalize: claiming a single test instantly proves death in every case
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Doctors use specific criteria to determine brain death, including the absence of reflexes, no change in pupil size, lack of response to painful stimuli, and inability to breathe on their own.
units.sources:
[1] Brain death
Sometimes, brain-dead people are kept alive with special machines and medications. For example, doctors can put a tube down a person's throat and use a machine called a ventilator to pump oxygen into their lungs. While these machines can keep the person's other organs alive for a while, they cannot help the brain get better. Eventually, the person's other organs will stop working too.

[2] Brain death
Diagnosis: Doctors can diagnose brain death by examining the patient. They will check for reflexes which are controlled by the brainstem, and see if the person can breathe on their own. If the person is brain-dead, the doctor will find:
- The person has no reflexes (for example, they do not gag when the doctor touches the back of their throat)
- The person's pupils do not change size in bright light or in the dark
- The person does not move or react when the doctor does something painful (like pinching the person's skin)
- The person does not try to breathe on their own

[3] Wikibooks: First Aid/Vitals
Purpose: As part of your ongoing assessment of the patient, and in preparation for the arrival of any assistance you have called, it is important to keep a check on a patient's vital signs to establish a baseline.

If possible, these recordings should be written down so that you can keep a record of any changes, and hand this over to the ambulance crew who take the patient from you. Ideally, it should be recorded on a report, which should form part of every first aid kit. Alternatively, you can write it on any piece of paper, or often first aiders end up writing on their protective glove.

units.question: Do carrots really sharpen your vision, or is it a myth?
units.gold: Mostly myth. The story was reportedly spread as wartime misinformation by the British RAF to hide a new technology used to shoot down German planes. The grain of truth: carrots contain beta-carotene and vitamin A, which the eyes need. In people with vitamin A deficiency, carrots can somewhat help night blindness, and beta-carotene may lower cataract and macular degeneration risk, but only at doses higher than a normal diet provides.
rubric: States carrots do not improve normal eyesight
Mentions the WWII RAF propaganda origin
Notes vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness that carrots can help
Mentions beta-carotene benefits only at high doses beyond normal diet
Penalize: claiming eating carrots corrects short-sightedness

The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Carrots do not sharpen vision; the myth originated during World War II to explain British pilots' ability to fight in the dark. Carrots contain beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, but this does not enhance vision in the dark.

units.question: Describe how drinking while pregnant can harm the baby.
units.gold: Alcohol crosses the placenta, and the baby's liver matures only late in pregnancy, so it cannot process alcohol at any stage. It can stunt growth, cause facial abnormalities and damage brain structures, leading to intellectual disability. The most severe outcome, from heavy drinking, is fetal alcohol syndrome: distinctive face (small eyes, small head, smooth area between nose and lip, thin upper lip), developmental and attention problems, poor memory, and possible heart, kidney, hearing and immune problems. Milder spectrum disorders (FASD) occur at lower drinking levels.
rubric: Explains alcohol crosses the placenta and the fetal liver cannot process it
Mentions growth restriction and brain damage
Describes fetal alcohol syndrome and its facial features
Mentions FASD at lower intake levels
Penalize: stating moderate drinking in pregnancy is proven safe
units.answer: Drinking alcohol during pregnancy can harm the baby by increasing the risk of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD), which can cause physical, behavioral, and learning problems [4]. It can also affect the baby's growth and increase the likelihood of birth defects. The risks are dose-dependent and can vary based on the amount and frequency of alcohol consumption.
units.sources:
[1] What can I do on a honeymoon in New Zealand while five months pregnant?
Tags: hiking, new-zealand We will be in New Zealand in April, the adventure capital of the world, but supposedly I can't do anything because I'm 5 months pregnant. Is there anything that I can actually safely do without risking harm to the baby? Baby comes first, even if it means that we'll just be like an elderly couple going on sightseeing cruises and taking photos sigh.

[2] What can I do on a honeymoon in New Zealand while five months pregnant?
Answers > Answer (score 14): Who says you can't hike?

If you have no medical concerns (ie high blood pressure, blood results showing complications etc) then guidance is to keep doing the sports you enjoy (with some exceptions - generally sports where impact or similar forces could cause injury - bungee jumping, motor racing etc - and those that could cause excess damage to ligaments, as these soften towards the later stages of pregnancy)

I don't know the two particular hikes you mention, but as long as you are aware of your water/food requirements and plan accordingly, there is nothing to stop you hiking as you normally would.

Kayaking may depend on the water - I wouldn't plan an extreme white water trip, but lake or calm seas or rivers may be fine - plan for more frequent stops and remain comfortable.

[3] What can I do on a honeymoon in New Zealand while five months pregnant?
Answers > Answer (score 14): Skiing is similar - don't plan on black runs, but you'll find many people ski on more moderate runs while pregnant. If you feel like you are comfortable doing it at 5 months then just do it. My wife was still running 10k runs at 8 months with one of our children, and did a 10k walk the day before my youngest was born.

Keeping fit and having regular exercise is considered a very good thing during pregnancy, so while you won't manage adrenaline sports, activities in general will be fine.

Plus: It's your honeymoon - have fun!

[4] Pregnancy and Substance Use (cited)
Other tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, also contain nicotine and are not safe to use during pregnancy. And some of the flavorings used in e-cigarettes may be harmful to developing babies.

You will also want to try to avoid secondhand smoke, which has some of the same risks as smoking during pregnancy.

Alcohol

There is no known amount of alcohol that is safe for you to drink during pregnancy and while trying to get pregnant. All types of alcohol are equally harmful, including all wines and beer. The risks from drinking during pregnancy include problems with the growth of the developing baby and fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD). FASD is a life-long condition that can cause a mix of physical, behavioral, and learning problems.

Illegal drugs

units.question: I've been eating very little for months. Can my basal metabolic rate actually slow down because of it?
units.gold: Yes. In the first few days of fasting, BMR actually rises, driven by catecholamines released as blood glucose falls and by high gluconeogenesis. As restriction continues, free T3 and catecholamine levels drop, gluconeogenesis slows and metabolic rate falls, largely through loss of lean tissue, especially muscle, while the body protects the glucose supply to the brain. Milder long-term restriction triggers the same adaptive processes on a smaller scale.
rubric: Confirms BMR decreases with prolonged calorie restriction
Mentions the initial short-term rise in BMR (catecholamines, gluconeogenesis)
Mentions falling free T3 and catecholamines later
Mentions loss of lean tissue/muscle as a main mechanism
Penalize: claiming metabolism never adapts to dieting
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Eating very little can lower your basal metabolic rate, as the body prioritizes survival functions over non-essential activities. This is a normal response to caloric deficiency. However, long-term malnutrition can lead to metabolic adaptations that may affect overall health.
units.sources:
[1] Metabolic rate
Basal metabolism: Basal metabolism is usually by far the largest component of total energy used. The release, and using, of energy in this state is sufficient only for the functioning of the vital organs, the heart, lungs, nervous system, kidneys, liver, intestine, sex organs, muscles, and skin.

[2] Metabolic rate
Metabolic rate is the rate of metabolism, the amount of energy used by an animal per unit of time. Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the amount of energy used daily by animals at rest. About 70% of a human's total energy use is due to the basal life processes within the organs of the body (see table). About 20% of one's energy use comes from physical activity and another 10% from the digestion of food after eating.

[3] Metabolic rate
Basal metabolism > Biochemistry: For the BMR, most of the energy is taken in keeping fluid levels up in tissues by osmosis, and only about one-tenth is used for mechanical work, such as digestion, heartbeat, and breathing.

What enables the Krebs cycle to perform metabolic changes to fats, carbohydrates, and proteins is energy, which can be defined as the ability or capacity to do work.

The breakdown of large molecules into smaller molecules – with release of energy – is catabolism. The breakdown of proteins into amino acids is an example of catabolism. Body heat in warm-blooded animals is produced by chemical reactions of the catabolic type.

The building up process is termed anabolism. The formation of proteins from amino acids is an anabolic process.

[4] How to trick my body/stomach into thinking I'm full?
Answers > Answer (score 14): The "trembling and weak" part suggests that you actually are low on blood sugar and aren't getting enough calories. I'd suggest you double check your calorie consumption and how much you actually eat. As someone said in the comments, those emergency rations might not get you as far as you think. So you might just be eating too little. But even then you can live on a calories deficit without feeling hungry. You "just" need to train your metabolism. Without regular cardio training, you body will prioritise metabolizing you glycogen storages in your muscles and relies on regular food supplies to replenish these. The body won't start burning a significant amount of fat before all those glycogen reserves are used up. For untrained people that is somewhere around 30 mins to an hour or so depending on the exercise.

What enables the Krebs cycle to perform metabolic changes to fats, carbohydrates, and proteins is energy, which can be defined as the ability or capacity to do work.

units.question: Can a blood antibody test show a past herpes type 2 infection in someone who never had symptoms, and how reliable is a positive?
units.gold: Yes, the HSV antibody test looks for the body's immune response rather than the virus, so it can pick up past, now inactive infections, though this depends on how long ago infection occurred. It is not 100% accurate. Its main weakness is missing infections (false negatives) rather than false positives; the false-positive rate in people without symptoms appears fairly low, but like any test it is not zero, so a positive does not prove infection with certainty.

[1] For countries requiring vaccination (especially USA) is there any allowance for an antibodies test, demonstrating natural immunity?
Answers > Answer (score 16): Another study published on Nov. This study found that the chances of these adults testing positive for COVID-19 were 5.49 times higher in unvaccinated people who had COVID-19 in the past than they were for those who had been vaccinated for COVID and had not had an infection before. They do not recognize any antibody test result as providing a sufficient level of protection: Data are presently insufficient to determine an antibody titer threshold that indicates when an individual is protected from infection.

[2] Herpes simplex
Symptoms: Usually, herpes is diagnosed based on the symptoms. There are tests that can confirm this diagnosis. Testing the blood for antibodies against the virus can confirm a previous infection but will be negative in new infections.

[3] Herpes simplex
Treatment: The disease is contagious, especially when it is active. Contagious means that it can spread from one person to another. There is no cure for this disease. This means that it cannot be stopped, once a person has got it. When a person has got the disease, he or she will get outbreaks from time to time. There are drugs that can make these outbreaks shorter, for many people. These antiviral drugs stop the virus from spreading. They will shorten the time people show symptoms.

[4] Why do countries check if arriving persons are vaccinated and not if they have antibodies?
Answers > Answer (score 43, accepted): Or see Can antibody tests tell you if a COVID-19 vaccine worked?:

A vaccinated person is very likely to get a negative result from a serology test, even if the vaccine was successful and protective. That’s because different serology tests detect antibodies to different parts of the virus.

Some tests detect antibodies to the spike protein of the virus, which are produced in response to viral infection or the vaccine. Others detect antibodies to a different part of the virus called the nucleocapsid protein, which are produced in response to infection, but not by the current vaccines.

MD Anderson’s Blood Bank uses an antibody test designed to detect antibodies to the nucleocapsid protein, which means donors who have received the COVID-19 vaccine will likely receive a negative antibody test result.

units.question: Is ice still recommended for minor burns, and what is the current first aid?
units.gold: No, ice is no longer advised because the extreme cold can injure tissue further. Calm the person and remove clothing not stuck to the burn (all of it if chemicals are involved). Cool the burn under cool running water for 10 to 15 minutes, or use a cool wet cloth or cool bath for about 5 minutes. Then check it is truly minor: deeper or larger burns, or burns on the hands, feet, face, groin, buttocks or major joints, need medical care right away. Leave blisters intact.

Advises not breaking blisters

units.answer: Ice should not be used for minor burns as it can cause further injury. First aid for minor burns includes cooling the burn with cool water and keeping the area clean. Some burns may require medical evaluation [1].

[1] Wikibooks: First Aid (cited)

[2] US government: Preventing and Treating Burns (Ready.gov)
- English Treat Minor Burns You can care for most minor first or second-degree burns at home. - First-degree burns affect only the thin top layer of skin.

[3] Wikibooks: First Aid (cited)
The intended audience is taking a first aid course from a certified instructor, and can read at a high school level. Please be advised that there are some images of the injuries and conditions discussed.

This is a wiki, so you can edit this book; and if you find a mistake, then please be bold and fix it. If you want to leave comments, please do so on the talk page for that module. If you want to help out even more, take a look through What needs to be done? for tasks that still need to be done, or start with whatever tasks you stumble across.

[4] Burn
Management > Intravenous fluids: f=== Wound care ===
Early cooling (within 30 minutes of the burn) reduces burn depth and pain, but care must be taken as over-cooling can result in hypothermia. It should be performed with cool water and not ice water as the latter can cause further injury. Chemical burns may require extensive irrigation. Cleaning with soap and water, removal of dead tissue, and application of dressings are important aspects of wound care. If intact blisters are present, it is not clear what should be done with them. Some tentative evidence supports leaving them intact. Second-degree burns should be re-evaluated after two days.

[5] Burn
Management > Alternative medicine: Honey has been used since ancient times to aid wound healing and may be beneficial in first- and second-degree burns. There is moderate evidence that honey helps heal partial thickness burns. The evidence for aloe vera is of poor quality. While it might be beneficial in reducing pain, and a review from 2007 found tentative evidence of improved healing times, a subsequent review from 2012 did not find improved healing over silver sulfadiazine. A 2014 review found only three randomized controlled trials for the use of plants for burns, two for aloe vera and one for oatmeal. The number of randomized control trials for aloe vera had increased to nine by 2024, when a review found a significant improvement in healing time but not pain relief.

units.question: What is the best way to avoid putting on frozen boots on a cold winter camping morning?
units.gold: Keep them in your sleeping bag overnight. Sweat accumulated in boots during the day freezes if they are left out, so you get boots that are both frozen and damp once thawed, which risks cold injuries such as trench foot over several days. Separate liners from shells and put both in the bag, or at least remove the insoles to help drying. Truly frozen heavy boots can be almost impossible to put on. Alternatives: vapour-barrier socks, or bottles of boiled water stuffed into the boots.

[2] How can I keep ingredients cold while camping?
Answers > Answer (score 28, accepted): Here is my camping strategy. If I'm going for more than a few days, here's what I do.

[3] How can I keep ingredients cold while camping?
Answers > Answer (score 28, accepted): - Start with a good air tight cooler. (Big enough to hold everything perishable). Forget those "gel packs". Definitely don't get a bag of ice from the convenience store. They melt and mess stuff up. Get a 2 litre bottle, rinse it out, fill it with water and freeze it. (Do this a couple days in advance, if possible). The less air in the better. This won't leak and will stay cold a good time as long as you don't open it.
- Take any raw meat that you're NOT planning on eating on the first day and freeze that too. Put the meat and all the frozen stuff at the bottom and to one side. My bottle of ice goes either directly on top of the meat or right beside it. This way, my meat has at least an extra day or two of grace and I don't need to waste extra space with an ice pack.
- Then layer stuff that isn't frozen, but can handle a little freezing on the next layer. Then work your way up, to any produce being on the top layer.

[4] Wikivoyage: Cold weather
Clothing: Pay great attention to footwear. Boots should be high enough to protect the ankle and for snow not to enter (preferably also protected in other ways). The sole must be thick enough and the boot itself and socks should be warm. Often a thick pair of socks is worn over a thin one, with the thick layer being wool or another type of expressly thermal socks (depending on boots this may be needed at -5 or -20°C). Use removable insulating insoles. The footwear must not be too tight, as that restricts blood flow (essential to keep the feet warm) and lessens trapped air (your main insulation). Near the freezing point boots must be protected from wet snow, e.g. by waxing. Below -5°C (23°F) moisture is less of a problem, but sunshine may still melt snow on the boots. Consider gaiters when loose snow is to be expected.

units.question: Describe a method for wading a knee-deep creek in winter and getting your feet warm and dry afterwards.
units.gold: A traditional military routine: pack gear in a waterproof sack and tie it up so it doubles as a buoyancy aid. Cross in your normal boots with thin socks and accept the cold. On the far side, remove wet boots and socks and bag them, then put on dry socks (with talcum powder) under waterproof Gore-Tex socks carried for this purpose, and put the wet boots back on: your foot heat dries them from inside while your feet stay dry. Absorbent nappies stuffed inside can help dry boots further.

Penalize: suggesting crossing barefoot on ice-covered rocks as the safest method
units.answer: Wade knee-deep in a winter creek, keep your footing, and dry your feet vigorously after reaching the other side [1]. Warm your feet with body heat or a small fire if necessary.

units.question: In a survival situation, can drinkable liquor like whiskey or vodka be used to clean a wound?
units.gold: Alcohol does kill germs, and 19th-century sources and at least one modern study support whiskey as an antiseptic. But alcohol should not be poured into an open wound, because it also kills exposed tissue and can delay healing. When no proper supplies are available, strong liquor can be used to clean dirt from the skin around a wound and to disinfect instruments. Antiseptics are for living tissue; disinfectants, which are harsher, are for surfaces and equipment.

[1] Could you use other liquors than vodka in pie dough?
Answers > Answer (score 4): Yes. We use apple jack in apple pie crust, which is a hard liquor with a sweet apple flavor. (As I recall, we took this idea from Alton Brown in an Apple Pie episode.) The apple jack provides the same benefit for flaky crust, and more apple flavor.

[2] Could you use other liquors than vodka in pie dough?
Answers > Answer (score 3): Judging by the recipe posted on Serious Eats, there are about 2 tablespoons of vodka per crust. Substituting two tablespoons of rum or other liquor may be enough to lend a minimum of fragrance, but I would not expect a strong flavor. I am not sure it would be perceptible in the over all flavor balance of the complete pie with its filling. You would need to use an extract (which is much stronger) to get a robust result.

On the other hand, if you are substituting for convenience because you don't have vodka conveniently available, as long as the proof or alcohol percentage is compatible to vodka, the chemistry will be the same.
