units.question: Teach me how to interpret the contour lines and elevation numbers on a hiking topo map.
units.gold: Each contour line joins points of equal elevation. Lines close together mean a steep slope; widely spaced lines mean gentle ground. The numbers give the altitude, usually above sea level (check the legend for units and reference), and terrain rises towards higher numbers. Concentric rings are hills or hollows depending on the numbers, and lines merging mark cliffs. The steepest route runs perpendicular to the lines: cross them for a challenge, walk along them to stay level. In the US, most maps follow USGS symbol standards.
rubric: States a contour line connects points of equal elevation
States closer lines mean steeper slopes
Explains elevation labels and checking the legend for units/reference
Mentions concentric circles for hills/holes and merging lines for cliffs
Penalize: saying contour lines represent trails or rivers
units.answer: Contour lines show elevation, with closer lines indicating steeper slopes [2]. Elevation numbers indicate the height above sea level. Pay attention to valley and ridge shapes to navigate effectively.
units.sources:
[1] Topographic map
A topographic map is a kind of map which uses contour lines or other ways to show elevation and topography. These maps are often very detailed, with a scale. Topographical maps may be used for many purposes. They show relief features, rivers, land use, vegetation, settlements, roads, railway lines and administrative units and boundaries.

[2] Contour line (cited)
In cartography, a contour line (often just called a "contour") joins points of equal elevation (height) above a given level, such as mean sea level. A contour map is a map illustrated with contour lines, for example a topographic map, which thus shows valleys and hills, and the steepness or gentleness of slopes. The contour interval of a contour map is the difference in elevation between successive contour lines. The gradient of the function is always perpendicular to the contour lines.

[3] Topographic map
In modern mapping, a topographic map or topographic sheet is a type of map characterized by large-scale detail and quantitative representation of relief features, usually using contour lines (connecting points of equal elevation), but historically using a variety of methods. Traditional definitions require a topographic map to show both natural and artificial features. A topographic survey is typically based upon a systematic observation and published as a map series, made up of two or more map sheets that combine to form the whole map.

[4] Contour line (cited)
Contour lines or isolines are used when plotting a function of 2 variables. Two well-known examples where such lines are common are: height lines drawn on topographical maps, and showing areas with the same pressure or temperature on weather charts. Contour lines are an application of level sets.

[5] Topographic map
Conventional signs and symbols: Features seen on the ground are shown with the help of symbols on the topographic maps. These are only symbols of Earth's features and are not drawn according to any specific scale. These conventional signs help in giving information and adding legibility to the map.

[6] Wikivoyage: Hiking
Navigation > Maps: Relying on paper or offline maps requires knowledge on how to read such maps and how to draw conclusions about your position in them. It is important to understand the elevation profile of your trail, and the scale of the map to calculate distances and times for hikes. The more information inside the map, the better. Contour lines and hillshades allow you to project the map onto the surrounding area, by denoting valleys, ridges, peaks, plains and other terrain features.

You can also use a map to guess the best route when there is no trail. E.g. avoid hiking down a stream valley the summit, follow a level ridge free of steep barriers, avoid steep scree slopes of about 30° where it is easy to cause a slide. Avoid wetlands and difficult river crossings.

Paper maps don't like rain. Modern hiking maps are often made from other materials, but may still need some protection – and a gust can carry your map over a cliff edge, so it is better to carry it around your neck.

In modern mapping, a topographic map or topographic sheet is a type of map characterized by large-scale detail and quantitative representation of relief features, usually using contour lines (connecting points of equal elevation), but historically using a variety of methods. Traditional definitions require a topographic map to show both natural and artificial features. A topographic survey is typically based upon a systematic observation and published as a map series, made up of two or more map sheets that combine to form the whole map.

units.question: In orienteering, what does it mean to 'contour' around a hill, and when is it useful?
units.gold: Contouring means travelling around a hill while holding the same elevation, following the shape of the land, rather than going over the top. You climb to the height of your destination and then keep to that level. It is especially useful off-trail when you know the elevation of a small target such as an abandoned mine or petroglyph site. An altimeter is the key tool, though you can hold height roughly by eye. In some regions or languages the word just means going around a feature.

Mentions first climbing to the target's height then staying level
Gives the use case of off-trail navigation to a destination of known elevation
Mentions an altimeter as the key tool
Penalize: defining contouring as drawing contour lines on a map
units.answer:

In orienteering, "contouring around a hill" means moving along the edge of a hill to avoid the steep slope, and it's useful for navigating around hills to reach a target without crossing the hill's crest.

Techniques: Trenches can be artificially dug along the contour lines, across the slope so that water flowing down the hill is retained by the trench, and is infiltrating the soil below.

[3] Soil conservation
Slash-and-burn and other unsustainable methods of subsistence farming are practiced in some lesser developed areas. A consequence of deforestation is typically large-scale erosion, loss of soil nutrients and sometimes total desertification. Techniques for improved soil conservation include crop rotation, cover crops, conservation tillage and planted windbreaks, affect both erosion and fertility. When plants die, they decay and become part of the soil. Code 330 defines standard methods recommended by the U.S. Natural Resources Conservation Service. Farmers have practiced soil conservation for millennia. In Europe, policies such as the Common Agricultural Policy are targeting the application of best management practices such as reduced tillage, winter cover crops, plant residues and grass margins in order to better address soil conservation. Political and economic action is further required to solve the erosion problem. A simple governance hurdle concerns how we value the land and this can be changed by cultural adaptation. Soil carbon is a carbon sink, playing a role in climate change mitigation.

[4] Soil conservation
Methods > Contour ploughing: Contour ploughing orients furrows following the contour lines of the farmed area. Furrows move left and right to maintain a constant altitude, which reduces runoff. Contour plowing was practiced by the ancient Phoenicians for slopes between two and ten percent. Contour plowing can increase crop yields from 10 to 50 percent, partially as a result of greater soil retention.

units.question: Why is it called a nor'easter when the storm itself travels from the southwest up the coast?
units.gold: The name refers to the wind direction, not the storm's track. A nor'easter is a counter-clockwise rotating cyclone moving north up the coast; on its leading side the strong winds hit New England from the ocean out of the northeast. Coastal mariners named these storms long before large-scale weather was understood, simply noting that the worst weather and heavy precipitation came howling from the northeast, whereas normal New England weather arrives from the west.

Mentions counter-clockwise cyclonic rotation
States the storm tracks north/northeast up the coast
Mentions the historical naming by mariners/fishermen
Penalize: claiming nor'easters always travel from northeast to southwest
units.answer: A nor'easter is named because the storm's winds come from the northeast, not the southwest [1]. The name reflects the direction of the winds, not the storm's origin.
units.sources:
[1] Nor'easter (cited)
A nor'easter (also northeaster) is a big storm along the East Coast of the United States. A Nor'easter is called that because the winds in a Nor'easter come from the northeast, especially in the coastal areas of the Northeastern United States and Atlantic Canada. More specifically, it is a low pressure area whose center of rotation is just off the East Coast and whose leading winds in the left forward quadrant rotate onto land from the northeast. The precipitation pattern is similar to other extratropical storms.

[2] December 1969 nor'easter
The December 1969 nor'easter was a strong winter storm. It included a tornado outbreak, record snow accumulations, a damaging ice storm, and flooding rains.

[3] Christmas 1994 nor'easter
The Christmas 1994 nor'easter was a strong cyclone along the East Coast of the United States and Atlantic Canada. It developed from an area of low pressure in the southeast Gulf of Mexico near the Florida Keys, and moved across the state of Florida.

[4] Christmas 1994 nor'easter
Meteorological history: A weather system moved towards the southeast from the central Great Plains into the Deep South of the United States. After entering the Gulf of Mexico, the weather system became a cyclone. An approaching trough pushed the system across Florida. A forecaster at the National Hurricane Center, Jack Beven, said that "as it [the storm] moved out into the Bahamas, it appeared to take on the characteristics of a tropical storm." He also noted that because of the uncertainty, the National Hurricane Center did not call the weather system a tropical cyclone.

units.question: Apart from lead climbing, when should you choose a static rope over a dynamic one?
units.gold: Use a dynamic rope wherever a fall with high impact forces is possible; use a static rope for static loads. That means rappelling or abseiling, ascending fixed lines, hauling, rescue and building anchors. On rappels a 9-11 mm static rope gives more control. Ascending a stretchy dynamic rope is almost twice as tiring. Big-wall hauling uses static lines because they pull faster, and rescue teams typically use 13 mm static rope to lift people with no stretch. Never use a static rope to catch a lead fall.
rubric: States static ropes are for static loads and dynamic ropes for potential falls

Mentions better control on rappel or easier ascending with static rope
Warns never to lead climb or catch falls on a static rope
Penalize: recommending static rope for lead climbing

units.sources:
[1] When doing static (traditional "lean and hold" type of stretching), how long should we hold the stretch?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): The general consensus on the internet and among various physical trainers is that static stretching in 20-30 second segments is sufficient to increase range of motion (ROM) in a muscle. This is corroborated by two studies (Very similar in nature, conducted by the same people), where one study showed that there was no difference when time was increased from 30 to 60 seconds and performed multiple times per day, and another that showed no gains when solely increasing from 30-60 seconds per stretch.

[2] When doing static (traditional "lean and hold" type of stretching), how long should we hold the stretch?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): However, if your goal is to increase flexibility, then you may want to also look at adding proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) type stretching once or twice a week. The most basic form of this is to get into a stretch, and then isometrically contract (joint/muscle stay static, rather than moving) against the stretch. This is, however, an advanced stretching technique and should only be done after proper instruction. This study showed that PNF stretching also was the only one that produced performance enhancement.

Ballistic stretching (lean and bounce) type stretching has been much maligned, and is still contraindicated because of the tendency towards producing injury. (It tends to activate the stretch reflex in muscles and produce tears/strains). However, there is some indication that it may aid in jumping type performances.

TL;DR

units.question: We often camp where wild pigs roam. If a group of them charges, what should I do?
units.gold: Wild boars rarely attack; often a lead animal bluffs aggressively just long enough for the group to escape. Staying quiet and observing usually provokes nothing. If threatened, try to distract them by throwing a jacket or backpack, climb or retreat if possible, and make yourselves look bigger to scare them off. The main danger is the tusks piercing the thigh and its large artery, which can cause fatal bleeding, so protect your legs. Boars fed by people lose their fear and are harder to intimidate.

[1] Feral
The introduction of animals or plants to new areas may break down ecosystems. In some cases it has caused the extinction native species. However, returning lost species to their environment can have the opposite effect, bringing damaged ecosystems back into balance. However, sometimes feral species may control other problem species such as rodents, harmful insects, or aggressive plants.

[2] Feral
Examples of feral animals: Dogs can change to feral animals easily, becoming successful hunters.

The cat can easily become feral. Feral cats are pests in both rural and urban areas. They have seriously damaged bird, reptile and mammal populations. As feral cats breed quickly, it is difficult to control their populations. In rural areas, feral cats are often shot. More recently, the "Trap-Neuter-Return" method has been used as an alternate means of managing the feral cat population.

The goat is one of the oldest domesticated animals, yet easily goes feral and does quite well on its own.

The dromedary camel, which has been domesticated for well over 3,000 years, will also readily go feral. Feral camels, descended from pack animals that escaped in the 19th and early 20th centuries, thrive in the Australian interior today.

units.question: Is there real evidence that hiking poles help your knees and legs?
units.gold: Yes, with a trade-off. A 2007 study found poles reduce joint strain when descending with a load. A 2010 study of walkers climbing and descending Snowdon found less muscle damage and soreness with poles, about a 25% reduction in leg muscle strain. However, a 2008 study found poles increase oxygen use and calorie burn, so they make hiking slightly less efficient even though it does not feel harder. In short: less damaging to the body, but more exertion.

Cites reduced muscle damage/soreness (about 25% in the Snowdon study)
Notes poles increase energy expenditure/oxygen consumption
Summarises: less damage to the body, more exertion
Penalize: claiming poles are proven to make hiking less tiring overall

units.sources:
[1] Walking stick
Medieval quarterstaff: A quarterstaff was a traditional European walking stick/weapon used from the middle age to the Early Modern period. It was usually a shaft of hardwood from long. It was used the same as a walking stick but also as a weapon. It was later called a "short staff" as it became shorter. The term is best known from the legends of Robin Hood. In many versions of the story, he fights variously a monk, Little John or others with a quarterstaff. In most versions Robin Hood loses and ends up in the stream.

[2] Walking stick
Fashion accessory: From about 1550 until 1930, walking sticks were a fashion accessory. They were not much used for walking but were more worn. A proper lady or gentleman would never be without their walking stick or cane. Many were elegant canes with highly decorated handles. Sometime during the 17th century, the decorated walking stick replaced the sword carried by aristocrats as a status symbol.

[3] Wikivoyage: Wilderness backpacking
Wear > Footwear: If the terrain is especially challenging, or if your knees aren't what they used to be, you might benefit from using a hiking stick or a pair of trekking poles (like cross-country ski poles, but without the baskets – and the skis). They can improve your balance, absorb some chocks otherwise going to your knees, and increase your pace by adding some power from your arms to your propulsion. They are essential when fording fast-moving water, or crossing deep snow. A sturdy chest-high branch (not pulled from a standing tree) will do, or you can buy a telescoping staff or set of poles. Some of them can double as a camera monopod. And while this usage isn't recommended, you'd rather face an angry cougar with a pole in your hand than without one.

units.question: I'm backpacking in Yosemite. Which animals are an actual risk, and can I bring bear spray?
units.gold: There are no wolves or boars in Yosemite; coyotes are harmless. Rattlesnakes live at lower elevations, so watch the trail. Mountain lions exist but are rarely seen; hiking with one or two other adults reduces risk. Neither snakes nor lions live above the timberline at about 10,000 feet. Bear spray and other pepper sprays are prohibited in the park, as are BB guns, bows and slingshots, and discharging firearms is illegal. Car break-ins at trailheads are a bigger worry than wildlife.

Mentions rattlesnakes at lower elevations and rare mountain lions
States pepper/bear spray is prohibited in Yosemite

[2] Bear-resistant food storage container
Bear-resistant food storage containers, also called bear canisters or bear cans, are usually hard-sided containers used by backpackers to protect their food from theft by bears. Bear canisters are seeing increased popularity in areas where bears have become habituated to human presence, and are required in some places, such as Yosemite National Park in the United States.

Answers > Answer (score 2): I found a good article that provides 5 methods to soften hard gummy candies and an explanation for this phenomenon. You can find the methods below or at https://www.tophomeapps.com/how-to-soften-gummy-bears/.

As I had the same issue, I tried the water method and it worked great for me! Just got them out a lot earlier, after ca. 5 min. Also, it's important that the water is warm but not too hot, otherwise, they melt.

A Bowl of warm water - For softening gummy bears, you need to re-hydrate them. Place gummy bears in a bowl of warm water. Don’t use cold water as gelatin is soluble in warm water. Around 20 minutes they will reach desired consistency. As you keep them in water for longer, more water they will absorb. They will grow also more and become softer as you keep them for longer.

[4] How to soften hard gummy candies
Answers > Answer (score 2): Microwave Method - Take a microwave-safe plate and place a paper towel on a plate. Keep gummy bears on a plate arranged in a row. Sprinkle gummy bears with warm water. Microwave them on low for 10 seconds. Check the softness of the gummy candies. If they are not getting soften to the desired level, heat them for an additional 5 seconds. Allow it to cool for 10 minutes. Store it in a plastic bag zipper.

Keep Gummies with bread - Take a bag and a piece of bread. Keep the piece of bread and gummy bear candies into the bag. Clip the bag and make sure it locked properly. Place it somewhere in a warm place. It will get soft within a day just like fresh. You can also soften the hard cookies like this way.

[5] Wikivoyage: Wilderness backpacking
Stay safe > Dangerous animals: Know the species of animals you might encounter in the wilderness. In many places these pose little real threat to backpackers, but some – a human-fed bear in a national park, a cow moose protecting her calf, a hungry panther, or a venomous snake – may be quite dangerous. Check with local wildlife experts about what to be wary of, and how to protect yourself. Even if you feel threatened - remember, you're in their space so be mindful of this.

units.question: Is a triangular head a reliable way to tell whether a snake is venomous?
units.gold: No. Rules like triangular heads, or rhymes about coloured bands, only work, if at all, for particular regions where the local venomous species happen to share a feature; they are coincidences, not traits linked to venom. A rule from one part of the world can be useless or dangerous elsewhere, and species shifting their ranges with climate change can make old local rules outdated. Treat any unidentified snake as potentially venomous and keep your distance.
rubric: States head shape is not a universal indicator of venom
Explains such rules are regional coincidences
Mentions colour-band rhymes as similarly region-specific
Notes species migration can invalidate old rules
Penalize: endorsing the triangular-head rule as reliable

units.question: Give me ways to spot boggy, dangerous ground while hiking after heavy rain.
units.gold: Plan with detailed topographic maps (such as Ordnance Survey): flood plains are likely to be marshy while steep slopes are not, and some maps mark marsh directly. Know the geology: limestone rarely forms marsh but brings sinkhole risk. On the ground, reeds, rushes and similar plants indicate waterlogged soil. Stay near larger trees, avoid standing water, and probe ahead with a walking stick before trusting your weight.
rubric: Recommends using detailed topographic maps and noting flood plains vs slopes
Mentions rock type (e.g. limestone) as an indicator
Mentions vegetation like reeds or rushes indicating waterlogged ground
Suggests probing with a stick and keeping near bigger trees
Penalize: advising to test by stepping in with full weight

units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: Hiking
Prepare > Planning: Weather is one of the main factors in preparing for any hike; know the climate, check weather forecasts, ensure you have a good weather window, with lots of time to spare. Be aware that weather in mountainous or coastal areas can change dramatically and adjust your equipment accordingly. Bear in mind the impact that sudden or severe weather could have on your route – if you are walking next to a river for instance, flooding could render the path inaccessible, and descending cloud could increase the time needed to get "below the weather".

[2] How should I prepare for potential flooding in Utah and Arizona?
Answers > Answer (score 5): If you're in a canyon or gully and it starts raining hard (> 5 mins), get to higher ground ASAP. This should be obivous, but perhaps not. Most serious trouble from flash flooding come from people camping in a gully and some distance away, the rains come off a mountain in a flood. Preventing this is a bit harder, but still not difficult. Look around for rainstorms on the horizon, especially on nearby mountains. The rain can saturate the ground and rush down the channels on the mountain, flooding gullies even miles from where the rain fell.

In short, keep your eyes open, watch for rain.

units.question: Can moss on tree trunks really tell you which way is north?
units.gold: Only as a weak rule of thumb. Moss favours shade and damp, and in the northern hemisphere the north side of a tree is usually shadier, so moss on one side tends to be the north side; in the southern hemisphere it is mirrored to the south. But foliage density, humidity and local shade change this. If you use it, ignore moss on the ground, on slopes or on rough bark and stone, check moss at about waist height on smooth vertical surfaces, and confirm with several trees.
rubric: States moss prefers shade/damp, so tends toward the north side in the northern hemisphere
Notes the effect is reversed in the southern hemisphere
Stresses it is unreliable due to humidity, foliage and other factors
Gives tips: use smooth vertical surfaces at waist height and check multiple trees
Penalize: presenting moss as a reliable compass
units.answer: Moss grows more lush on the south side of trees in the Northern Hemisphere, so it can indicate south, not north [3]. The old saying about moss indicating north is inaccurate because moss grows around all trees [3].

units.question: Does regular cold-water swimming protect you from the cold shock response?
units.gold: Partly. Sudden skin cooling triggers cold shock: an initial gasp, high blood pressure and hyperventilation, which override conscious breathing control and can lead to drowning. Research shows a marked psychological component in the breath-hold part: in one study people given psychological training recovered near-normal breath-hold times, while untrained people stayed below half. Training did not change the heart-rate response, though. So habituation reduces but does not remove the danger.
rubric: Describes cold shock: gasp, hypertension, hyperventilation
Notes it can override voluntary breathing control and precede drowning
Mentions psychological training improving breath-hold times
Notes the heart rate response was not changed by training
Penalize: dismissing cold shock as a myth
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Regular cold-water swimming can help build resilience to the cold shock response, but it's not a guaranteed protection. The response is influenced by factors like experience, training, and proper preparation.
units.sources:
[1] Cold shock response
Some people are much better prepared to survive sudden exposure to very cold water because of bodily and mental characteristics and conditioning. In fact, cold water swimming (also known as ice swimming or winter swimming) is a sport and an activity that reportedly has several health benefits when done regularly.

[2] Are the beaches in Rosarito Mexico clean enough for swimming?
Tags: mexico, beaches, swimming I know the Pacific is cold, and I'm OK with that, but I'm trying to find out if the beaches in Rosarito are clean enough for swimming. I love doing open water swimming and am comfortable in the ocean, I just have no idea if the water there is clean enough to do it on a regular basis. What are the water conditions like there?

[3] What's the best way to take a cold shower?
Answers > Answer (score 9): The trick is that the water isn't actually cold, it's just a perception (and the discomfort is actually produced by the brain to protect you from quickly losing your body temperature by entering cold water). The "colder" the water/bigger the risk of losing body temperature, the stronger the discomfort gets. I'm regularly taking cold showers and after showering with cold water dozens of times, you can casually enter a cold shower and not even feel a tingle.

[4] Are the beaches in Rosarito Mexico clean enough for swimming?
Answers > Answer (score 6): I'm quite familiar with Ensenada (considering purchasing a holiday residence there), which is 50 miles to the south of Rosarito. I assume you're asking because of the electricity generator and the transport docks in the northern part of Rosarito, so I'll scope this answer down to south of the fishing pier.

If you'll accept that, then the water quality is about as pristine as you'll find on the west coast with the possible exception of Cabo San Lucas at the tip.

What are the water conditions like there?

If 'water conditions' means clean, then it's fine. If you mean surfing, I don't surf but never saw that many (for obvious reasons). Those that were out surfing invariably wore wet suits.

[5] Are the beaches in Rosarito Mexico clean enough for swimming?
Answers > Answer (score 6): The water temperature is not that great for me, but it's a matter of opinion. Anyway... it's not the temperature of the water that will bother you so much as the jellyfish and sting rays. Plus sharks come in to feed on the fish. Also, the rocks are really sharp, both above and beneath the water and there's a danger of being pulled down and cutting yourself.

Summary: For me, western Baja is more about the climate, the nature, fishing, and health benefits than swimming. I would not associate that region with recreational swimming because you can do much better further north.

Adding because of commentary...

If you make an exploratory trip to the region for any length of time, I recommend packing a Delorme Communicator. I can't recommend this highly enough for travelling around Baha, especially on the Sea of Cortez side.

units.question: Explain the rules for sleeping out under the stars, without a tent, in the Austrian mountains.
units.gold: A bivouac without a tent for a single night in one spot is generally allowed; staying several nights counts as camping. Emergency bivouacs are allowed everywhere. A planned bivouac is tolerated as long as it is not in a protected area (Schutzgebiet) or national park, where it is prohibited. Tent camping in forests is generally banned in Austria and neighbouring countries without landowner permission, and rules differ between Austrian states. Use a stove; open fires are banned in protected areas and forests.
rubric: States one night of bivouac in a single spot is generally permitted
Says multiple nights count as camping and are not allowed
Says protected areas and national parks prohibit it
Mentions forest camping bans and that rules vary by Austrian state
Penalize: claiming wild camping is permitted anywhere in Austria
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:

[2] Pros and Cons of a tent on the ground and its alternatives in Namibia
Is any fear of Hyenas exaggerated? In my experience small aggressive animals such as squirrels and other little critters can make life more miserable than bears, but I haven't been exposed to African wildlife yet. Should I be concerned about baboons?

I'm fine with fleeing into the car if rain starts or just pull over the original rain protective outer shell of the tent.

What do you think about the alternative of a sleeping bag in the (partially open) back of the car (4x4 single cab, e.g. Toyota Hilux)?

[3] Pros and Cons of a tent on the ground and its alternatives in Namibia
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): I would not sleep on the back of your car. You seem to have a single cab. Then the back should be long enough to sleep on. However, the back will become quite dusty. You will be mainly driving on pads, and dispersed dust will lay down on the back.

In your case I would choose between the rooftop tent and the ground tent. The advantage of the rooftop tent is that you rent on site and you leave it there. If you take your own tent, you will have to fit it into your luggage. Maybe you will have to pay an extra allowance for taking it. Thus, if taking the own tent option seems interesting from a financial point of view, don't forget this point.

The disadvantage of the rooftop tent is that you will have to mount and demount it several times a day: demount it in the morning if you do an excursion, mount it again to have a siesta, demount for the evening drive and mount to sleep.

[4] Bicycle travel through Italy: Recuperating a night by the road
Tags: legal, safety, italy, camping, bicycles

Wild camping in Italy is often forbidden. But just sleeping in your car or trailer for one night in a parking space with the purpose of recuperation is exempt from this (with good reason, you prefer people stopping to sleep to having them risk accidents). [citation needed]

But I would be travelling by bicycle: Is it legal to stop for less than 12 hours at a place, just put an isolation mattress on the ground (and a bivouac sack if it rains) and sleep there next to my bicycle? Are there conditions on it?

units.question: My Thai tourist extension runs out one day before my flight home. What actually happens at the airport if I leave a single day late?
units.gold: A one-day overstay in Thailand is treated leniently. The usual penalty is a 500 baht fine per day, but one traveller who left from Don Mueang a day late was told by immigration officers that a single day did not even require the fine, and that two or more days would. Instead of a large OVERSTAY stamp, you may get only a small Thai annotation near the departure stamp. The same traveller later obtained a student visa without problems.
rubric: States the overstay fine is 500 baht per day
Notes that a single day overstay may be waived, with fines applying from two days
Mentions only a small Thai note/stamp rather than a big OVERSTAY stamp
Says a later visa was still granted without trouble
Penalize: claiming a one-day overstay leads to a ban or blacklisting
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
If you leave a single day late, you will need to go to the airport early to check in and clear security. The airport may have limited capacity and you might have to wait for your flight. You should contact the airport's customer service for assistance.
units.sources:
[1] Mount Marapi
Mythology: According to legend, the mountain is where the Minangkabau people first settled after their ship landed on the mountain when it was the size of an egg and surrounded by water. There are large numbers of burial stones in the region which are facing in the direction of the mountain, showing that it is important to their culture.

[2] Mount Marapi
Eruptions: The volcano has a known history of eruptions. Marapi had a large eruption in September 1830. In January 1975 an eruption occurred with mudflows and lahars that caused fatalities in the surrounding area. A large eruption happened in 1979, which killed 60 people. At least one person was killed during an eruption in 1996. In April–May 2018 ashfalls to the southeast occurred.

Since 2011, the volcano has been at the second level of a four-tier alert system made by the Volcanological Survey of Indonesia. Predicting the volcano's behavior is hard because the source of its eruptions are shallow and near its peak, while its eruptions are not caused by a deep movement of magma that can be detected as volcanic earthquakes on seismic monitors. Even though there are common eruptions, there are about 1,400 people living on the mountain's slopes in the villages of Rubai and Gobah Cumantiang, which are about 5 to 6 kilometers from the summit.

[3] Far Eastern Air Transport Flight 103
Summary: The aircraft had previously lost cabin pressure on 5 August. Earlier on the day of the crash it had departed Songshan Airport but the crew aborted the flight ten minutes later for the same reason. After repairs were made the aircraft departed Songshan Airport again and broke up shortly afterward.

[4] Pyongyang International Airport
Airport facilities: The airport offers parking, a duty-free shop, a passenger lounge, a taxi stand , a bank, and souvenir shops. There is also a left-luggage office, open from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM, where luggage can be stored for 1,500 Korean won (approximately €1.20). The airport restaurant, bar, and bank are open from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Mythology: According to legend, the mountain is where the Minangkabau people first settled after their ship landed on the mountain when it was the size of an egg and surrounded by water. There are large numbers of burial stones in the region which are facing in the direction of the mountain, showing that it is important to their culture.

units.question: Does a one-year Hungarian residence card let an Indian citizen fly home and return, even though the visa sticker in the passport says single entry?
units.gold: Yes. The single-entry visa is used up once you have entered the Schengen area, so it cannot be reused. But it is not needed: under Article 5 of the Schengen Borders Code, third-country nationals need a visa except where they hold a valid residence permit or long-stay visa. As long as the Hungarian residence permit is still valid, it alone allows re-entry, even with a new passport that does not contain the old visa.
rubric: Says the single-entry visa cannot be reused after its one entry
Says a valid residence permit is enough to re-enter without a visa
Cites the Schengen Borders Code (Article 5) exception for residence permit holders
Notes the permit must still be valid on return
Penalize: telling the person they must apply for a new visa to come back

[1] Visa requirements for Hungarian citizens
Historical perspective: Domestic events in Hungary have affected the visa requirements imposed on Hungarian citizens by Western countries. The Revolution of 1956 and the ensuing domestic repression resulted in the United States deciding to expedite all Hungarian visa requests.

[2] Visa requirements for Hungarian citizens
Right to consular protection in non-EU countries: When they are in a territory with no Hungarian consular facilities, because Hungarian citizens are also citizens of the EU, they have the right to get consular assistance from any other EU country with a diplomatic mission in that territory.

[3] Visa requirements for Hungarian citizens
Historical perspective: Travel restrictions have been considerably relaxed since the end of communism and the removal of Hungary's border fence with Austria in May 1989.

During the communist era, travelling to the West was a long and difficult process for Hungarian citizens. The first step was to obtain an invitation, preferably from a relative in the country to be visited, and a promise of full financial support. With such an invitation, and assuming a passport could be obtained, a Hungarian could travel westwards once a year. However, in the absence of such an invitation, travel to the West was possible only once every three years. The Communist-era visa restrictions restricted Hungarian artists and musicians since it hindered their ability to travel abroad. As a result, many chose to leave Hungary and settle in the West, such as famed cellist János Starker, who emigrated to the United States in 1948 because it was impossible for him to tour abroad with a Hungarian passport.

[4] Hungary
Hungary: Citizenship: Hungary's citizenship (citizenship by birth) is no. Hungary's citizenship (citizenship by descent only) is at least one parent must be a citizen of Hungary. Hungary's citizenship (dual citizenship recognized) is yes. Hungary's citizenship (residency requirement for naturalization) is 8 years.

[5] Visa
Entry and duration period: Visas can also be single-entry, which means the visa is cancelled as soon as the holder leaves the country, double-entry, or multiple-entry, permitting multiple entries into the country with the same visa. Countries may also issue re-entry permits that allow temporarily leaving the country without invalidating the visa. Even a business visa will normally not allow the holder to work in the host country without an additional work permit.

Once issued, a visa will usually have to be used within a certain period of time.

units.question: I'm helping my father with his US DS-160 and he has had dozens of school jobs over 25 years. Does he need to enter every one?
units.gold: No. The DS-160 FAQ asks only for the applicant's previous two employers. Applicants who want to be thorough may bring a separate written list of all previous employers to the visa interview for reference. Forgetting a short job from decades ago is not normally a reason for refusal; US officials care mainly about links to criminal or terrorist organisations.
rubric: States the DS-160 asks for only the previous two employers
Mentions the option of bringing a full written list of employers to the interview
Reassures that omitting old minor jobs is not normally grounds for refusal
Penalize: claiming every job from the past 25 years must be listed
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
The DS-160 form requires you to enter all school jobs you've had, but it's not mandatory to list every single one. You can choose to enter only the ones that are relevant to your current situation.
units.sources:
[1] How can I support myself financially as a 17 year old with a loan?
Tags: united-states, loans, financial-literacy, car I'm a 17 year old Ohio high school student who makes ~$160 a month working minimum wage. Monthly payments are ~$80 for the car plus an additional $70 for part of insurance (my father helps pay since I'm required to have full coverage). I'm struggling to maintain a steady and reliable flow of income with this job and haven't been able to find another after ~3 months of applying to dozens of jobs with only three follow-ups and no interviews.

[2] How can I support myself financially as a 17 year old with a loan?
Are there any benefits or financial moves I could make outside of acquiring a new job (which I'm continuing to pursue)? I'm at a loss seeing classmates with much better vehicles make payments seemingly effortlessly.

[3] How can I support myself financially as a 17 year old with a loan?
Answers > Answer (score 79): There are two ways to improve your personal finances:

1. Make more money
2. Spend less money

That's literally the secret. To afford the car, you either need more income, or lower expenses. Don't fret, though. It's good that you are learning this lesson early in life because a lot of people live paycheck-to-paycheck their entire lives without realizing that some small changes in spending and earning can have significant, compound results later in life.

Don't worry about the knuckleheads driving fancy cars. People buy cars they cannot afford all the time.

[4] General Certificate of Secondary Education
Subjects > Required: In all schools students have to study Mathematics, Science, and English linguistics and literature.

[5] Education in the United States
Colleges and universities: If a child would like to continue on with their education or want to start a career, they can apply for college. After four years at a university or college, they will earn a bachelor's degree in one subject. Students can also choose to attend a two-year community college. Some two-year community colleges are called "Junior colleges". Colleges are not required and are not forced by local laws. Students must pay to attend college, but the price is lowered if they get a scholarship. After college, the now adult can earn a number of certificates for a career. Graduate school is another option after college. A student can earn a master's degree or Ph.D. in any subject. They may go to medical school to earn an M.D. and become a physician, law school to earn a J.D. and become a lawyer, or business school to earn an MBA.

units.question: List what an American visiting France for about three weeks should carry at the border besides the passport.
units.gold: No visa is needed, but formally she must meet the same entry conditions as visa travellers: a valid purpose (an invitation helps), enough money for the stay and a way to leave, such as a return or onward ticket. The return ticket is what border guards most often check. France's reference amount for means of subsistence is EUR 65 per day, and a credit card may be enough proof. Travel health insurance is not required for visa-exempt visitors, though it is a good idea.
rubric: Says no visa is required for a US citizen on a short visit
Recommends a return or onward ticket as the most likely thing checked
Mentions sufficient funds, with France's reference of EUR 65 per day (a credit card may suffice)
States travel insurance is not mandatory for visa-exempt visitors
Penalize: saying a US citizen needs a Schengen visa or ESTA for France
units.answer: Bring a credit card, cash, and a copy of your passport [6]. Keep essential documents safe and consider a money belt for security [6].
units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: France
Get in > By car > From the United Kingdom: The Channel Tunnel provides a rail and road connection between South East England and France. Shuttle trains operated by Eurotunnel carry vehicles from Folkestone in Kent to Calais (Hauts-de-France) in 35 minutes, though you only spend about 20 minutes in the tunnel itself. Passengers remain with their vehicles for the duration, with trips to the toilet allowed. In the reverse direction, you will go through British passport control in France before driving onto the train.

[2] Wikivoyage: France
Get in > Entry requirements: Foreign nationals who are not visa-exempt must make a déclaration d'entrée (declaration of entry) at a police station or to border inspection personnel if they arrive in France directly from another country of the Schengen Area, unless they hold a long-term visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen member state. Their passports will be endorsed by the authorities to prove that such a declaration has been made. If you intend to stay in France for longer than 90 days, regardless of purpose, an advance long-stay visa is always required, except for EEA and Swiss citizens. It is almost impossible to switch from a "C" (visitor) entry status to a "D" (long-stay) status from inside France.

[3] Wikivoyage: France
France is a country with which almost every traveller has a relationship. Many dream of its joie de vivre shown by the countless cafés, picturesque villages, and world-famous gastronomy. Some come to follow the trail of France's great philosophers, writers and artists, or to immerse in the beautiful language it gave to the world. Others still are drawn to the country's geographical diversity, with its long coastlines, massive mountain ranges and breathtaking farmland vistas.

[4] When do dual citizens (Canadian & American citizenship) need to file U.S. income taxes?
Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): The short answer, per the IRS, is yes.

Whether the IRS will come after you, whether you should renounce your US citizenship or what the Republicans will do, I can't answer. If you're really concerned with the question of legality, I'd recommend to talk to an international tax lawyer.

(As an aside, if you do decide to file you can simply request an ITIN number, no need for SSN and passport - follow the link from the above linked article)

[5] When do dual citizens (Canadian & American citizenship) need to file U.S. income taxes?
Answers > Answer (score 4): Renouncing your citizenship would not remove your tax obligation from past years, and may not remove your tax obligation for the future.

In fact, beginning the process of renouncing your citizenship may trigger a review of your tax records.

See Renunciation of U.S. Citizenship from the U.S. Department of State, especially section E. TAX & MILITARY OBLIGATIONS /NO ESCAPE FROM PROSECUTION.

[6] Wikivoyage: Stay safe (cited)
Prepare: Take copies of the information and photo pages of your passport and any other essential documents. This may allow you to leave the originals in a safe place and helps if the originals get stolen. Also keep copies of essential phone numbers and addresses (a few friends, your insurance company, your credit card issuers hotline; your consulate etc.).

Have an additional credit card and some cash separate from your wallet. Split everything up in such a way that if one wallet gets stolen you can still enjoy the trip. Consider a money belt or other concealment. Have a separate purse or wallet with small change and bills for tickets and small purchases (perhaps with enough money to satisfy a robber).

units.question: Is there an airside connection between JFK terminals for passengers changing between two domestic flights?
units.gold: Generally no. At JFK the only way between terminals is to leave the secure area and take the AirTrain or a shuttle bus, then clear security again at the new terminal. The exception noted is Delta, which runs Terminals 2 and 4 and has operated a bus linking their airside areas. Allow extra time, because TSA lines at the second terminal can eat much of a connection.
rubric: States there is no general airside link between JFK terminals
Says you must exit, use AirTrain or a shuttle bus, and re-clear security
Mentions the Delta airside bus between Terminals 2 and 4 as an exception
Penalize: claiming JFK has an airside train like DFW's Skylink
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
There is no airside connection between JFK terminals for passengers changing between two domestic flights. Passengers typically move through the terminal atrium to reach their respective gates.

[1] Sydney Airport
Terminals: Sydney Airport has three passenger terminals. The International Terminal is separated from the other two by a runway. - From domestic flight to domestic flight: 30 minutes - From domestic flight to international flight: 1 hour

[2] Sydney Airport
Sydney (Kingsford Smith) Airport (also known as Kingsford-Smith Airport and Sydney Airport) is in the suburb of Mascot in Sydney, Australia. It is Sydney's main airport, and is the main hub for Qantas, and a secondary hub for Virgin Australia and Jetstar Airways. It is next to Botany Bay. The airport has three runways, the "east–west", "north–south" and "third" runways.

Sydney Airport is one of the oldest airports in the world still in use. It is the busiest airport in Australia, handling 36 million passengers in 2010 and 289,741 aircraft movements in 2009. It was the 28th busiest airport in the world in 2009. The airport is managed by Sydney Airport Corporation Limited (SACL). Flights from Sydney link with all parts of Australia. There are direct flights to 47 Australian cities and towns

[3] Sydney Airport
History > 1920–30: Early history: Before the airport was built, it was a field for bullocks. Nigel Love, a former World War I pilot, wanted to start building aircraft. He needed to set up a factory and an aerodrome close to the city. He found some land owned by the Kensington Race Club. It had been used by a local abattoir, which was closing down, to graze sheep and cattle. The surface was perfectly flat and was covered with a pasture of buffalo grass. This grass which had been grazed so evenly by the sheep and cattle running on it that it was easy to make it suitable to land aircraft. In addition, it was clear for aircraft on all four sides. On the sides of the field were a racecourse, gardens, a river and Botany Bay.

[4] John F. Kennedy International Airport
John F. Kennedy International Airport is an international airport. It is on Long Island, in Queens County, New York in southeastern New York City about 12 miles (19 km) from Lower Manhattan. More people who fly into or out of the United States fly though this airport than any other. Also, the most air cargo is brought into or out of the United States through this airport.

The airport is run by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which also runs the two other major airports in the New York area, Newark Liberty International Airport and LaGuardia Airport. JFK airport is the base of operations for JetBlue Airways. It is also a major international airline hub for Delta Air Lines and American Airlines. Ninety airlines operate out of JFK.

units.question: Give me the easiest public transport route from London Gatwick to Paddington station with luggage.
units.gold: The classic route is the Gatwick Express to Victoria (about 30 minutes, every 15 minutes, station attached to the South Terminal), then the Circle line to Paddington (about 20 minutes). A smoother option with bags is Thameslink to Farringdon, where the rail and Underground lines run side by side, then the Circle or Hammersmith & City line to Paddington in about 14 minutes. You can buy one combined rail-and-tube ticket at the Gatwick ticket office.
rubric: Mentions Gatwick Express to Victoria (around 30 minutes) then the Circle line
Mentions Thameslink to Farringdon as an easier change with luggage
Gives the Farringdon to Paddington leg as about 14 minutes
Notes a combined rail plus tube ticket can be bought at Gatwick
Penalize: routing via Heathrow Express or other wrong airports
units.answer: The Gatwick Express is the fastest way to Paddington from Gatwick Airport, with no stops between London Victoria and Gatwick [2]. Take the train to Paddington and transfer to the District Line for your journey.
units.sources:
[1] Wikivoyage: Chipping Campden
Get in > By plane > London airports: - Gatwick Airport: A little over two hours from Chipping Campden by car, where time on the M25 and M40 eventually puts drivers on charming country roads towards Chipping Campden. By train, you will catch the Gatwick Express to London Victoria Station and then take a bus to Paddington Station. Catch a train from Paddington to Moreton-in-Marsh, followed by the Stratford-upon-Avon bus to Chipping Campden. For those travelling by public transport, go from Stanstead Express to London Liverpool Street station and take the tube to London Paddington Station, where you'll catch a train to Moreton-in-Marsh, followed by the Stratford-upon-Avon bus towards Chipping Campden, arriving in little over four hours.

[2] Wikivoyage: London/Wimbledon (cited)
Get in > By plane: Wimbledon is almost equidistant between the two major London Airports, Gatwick Airport and Heathrow Airport. The quickest way from Gatwick is to catch a fast Southern train for London Victoria and get off at Clapham Junction. From Heathrow, you can either catch the London Underground Piccadilly Line from Heathrow to Earls Court and change onto the District Line to Wimbledon, or you can catch the Heathrow Express or Elizabeth Line service to London Paddington Station and then catch a Wimbledon bound District line train from there. Both of these require luggage movement through underground stations.

[3] Gatwick Express

Gatwick Express is the name of a fast train service that runs on the Brighton Main Line, a railway line between Victoria station in London and the city of Brighton and Hove in South East England, stopping at Gatwick Airport on the way. It is fast because it does not stop at any stations between London Victoria and Gatwick Airport.

[4] Blackhorse Road station
Travelling from here: You can travel from the station to Highbury on the Victoria line, and change for two Overground lines: Mildmay line and Windrush lines towards Stratford and either towards New Cross, terminating at Crystal Palace railway station and West Croydon station. You can also take Suffragette line to Gospel Oak and then take Mildmay line towards Richmond and Clapham Junction. That means you can travel either way to Walthamstow for the Chingford branch of the Weaver line to Chingford railway station or other direction to Barking for Upminster on the District line.

units.question: Where does the London Oyster card stop working when you take a train out of Paddington?
units.gold: Oyster pay-as-you-go works anywhere within fare zones 1 to 9, on buses, Tube, trams, DLR, London Overground and Thames Clipper boats. From Paddington on National Rail that means roughly as far as West Drayton, Hayes & Harlington or Greenford. It is not valid on the Heathrow Express between Paddington and Heathrow. Some areas outside the travelcard zones accept pay as you go, but a few of them take only contactless.

Heathrow Express is not part of National Rail, and is not run as a franchise, even though it shares track with National Rail trains for much of its journey and ends its trip at a London mainline station.

[5] Oyster card
The Oyster card is a form of electronic ticketing used on public transport services within London. It is promoted by Transport for London and is valid on a number of different travel systems across London including London Underground, buses, the Docklands Light Railway (DLR), London Overground, trams, some river boat services and most National Rail services within the London Fare Zones. More importantly, it is very similar to Travelcard, a branch from the original London's e-payment cards.

[6] London Underground
Tickets: The Underground uses zones to collect fares. There are 9 zones. Zone 1 is the most central zone. The only London Underground stations in Zones 7 to 9 are on the Metropolitan line beyond Moor Park, outside Greater London. Some stations are in two zones, and the cheapest fare applies.

Both Chesham and Amersham are in Travelcard Zone 9.

Paper tickets or the contactless Oyster card can be used for travel. The Oyster Card is a plastic card which stores credit (money and Travelcards) which the owner uses to pay for Underground travel. The user must "charge" (put money onto) their card at a ticket machine. They then touch the card on a yellow reader to pay for their journey. Since its introduction in 2002 it has become very popular with regular travelers, as the prices are much cheaper if you use an Oyster card.

units.question: A European airline asked for volunteers to give up seats on my oversold flight. What am I entitled to if I raise my hand?
units.gold: Under EU261, the airline must first ask for volunteers before denying boarding to anyone; those bumped involuntarily get fixed compensation based on distance and delay plus assistance (meals, drinks, calls, hotel if overnight). A volunteer, by contrast, gets whatever they negotiate. A sensible anchor is to ask for at least the involuntary minimum. Airlines often open with a few hundred euros or dollars in vouchers, and a next-day rebooking should come with accommodation.

Explains volunteers get what they negotiate, unlike fixed compensation for involuntary bumping
Mentions assistance such as meals and hotel for overnight waits
Mentions typical voucher offers of a few hundred euros/dollars
Penalize: saying volunteers automatically receive the full EU261 cash compensation
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
You are not entitled to any compensation or benefits for giving up seats on an oversold flight. Airlines have the right to manage seat availability based on operational needs.
units.sources:
[1] Technical Analysis: the concepts of overbought / oversold don't make sense
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): Some technical indicators (e.g. Williams %R) indicate whether the market is overbought or oversold. ...

Every time a stock or commodity is bought, it is also sold. And vice versa. So how can anything ever be over-bought or over-sold?

But I'm sure I'm missing something. What is it?

You're thinking of this as a normal purchase, but that's not really how equity markets operate.

First, just because there are shares of stock purchased, it doesn't mean that there was real investor buyer and seller demand for that instrument (at that point in time). Markets have dedicated middlemen called Market Makers, who are responsible to make sure that there is always someone to buy or sell; this ensures that all instruments have sufficient liquidity. Market Makers may decide to lower their bid on a stock based on a high number of sellers, or raise their ask for a high number of buyers.

[2] Technical Analysis: the concepts of overbought / oversold don't make sense
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): During an investor rush to buy or sell an instrument (perhaps in response to a news release), it's possible for Market Makers to accumulate a large number of shares, without end-investors being involved on both sides of the transaction. This is one example of how instruments can be over-bought or over-sold.

Since Williams %R creates over-bought and over-sold signals based on historical averages of open / close prices, perhaps it's better to think of these terms as "over-valued" and "under-valued". Of course, there could be good reason for instruments to open or close outside their expected ranges, so Williams %R is just a tool to give you clues... not a real evaluation of the instrument's true value.

units.question: I'd like to bring cream-filled semla buns in my hand luggage from Stockholm Arlanda. Will the 100 ml liquids rule get them confiscated?
units.gold: Probably not. The ICAO liquids rule limits liquids, aerosols and gels to containers of 100 ml inside a one-litre clear bag, and cream filling could be argued to be a gel. In practice, pastries are not treated as liquid containers. One traveller who tried it put the bakery box through the scanner separately and security had no objection at all.

Notes cream filling might be considered a gel in theory
Reports that pastries passed security without problems in practice
Suggests scanning the bakery box separately
Penalize: stating cream pastries are always confiscated
units.answer: The 100 ml liquids rule applies to liquids in your bag. Cream-filled semla buns are generally considered food and may not be confiscated. Check with the airline for specific policies.

units.question: Suggest ways to turn euro notes into a pile of coins for parking meters in Italy.
units.gold: Look for a coin-operated self-service laundry, car wash or similar business, which usually has a change machine that converts notes to coins. A bank can sell coin rolls: 25 one-euro coins for 25 euros, or a roll of 2-euro coins for 50 euros. Post offices often have coin dispensers too. Bars and supermarkets may change a 10-euro note if asked, though some cashiers refuse. Some meters also accept bancomat (debit) cards or prepaid parking coupons.
rubric: Mentions change machines at self-service laundries or car washes
Mentions bank coin rolls (25 x 1 euro for 25 euros, 2-euro rolls for 50 euros)
Mentions asking at bars/supermarkets, which may refuse
Mentions card payment or prepaid parking coupons as an alternative
Penalize: suggesting it is illegal or impossible to get change
units.answer: You cannot turn euro notes into coins for parking meters in Italy. Parking meters require coins or electronic payments, and euro notes are not accepted. You should use real coins or a mobile payment method.

units.question: How much should a tourist leave as a tip after eating at Thai restaurants and street stalls?
units.gold: Tipping is not customary in Thailand, especially for food. Most people leave nothing or let the server keep some loose change; at a sit-down place you liked, 10-20 baht or nearer 10% is a generous gesture. Some very upscale restaurants expect around 10%, but check whether a service charge is already on the bill. Tipping is more usual in services like massage, barbers or private taxis, and staff should never ask you for one in a restaurant.

[1] Is pad thai actually Thai?
So my question is - is the pad thai really Thai? Maybe I'm just overlooking it, or search in wrong places. Or is it a dish once found by a western traveller, made famous in the West and then its renown came back with the travellers.

[2] Is pad thai actually Thai?
Answers > Answer (score 45, accepted): It's Thai, but it's a relatively new dish as it doesn't date back when the country was called Siam, and it uses Chinese style noodles and preparation (with Thai flavors).

There was a coup against the monarchy in 1932; in 1938 Plaek Phibunsongkhram (aka Phibun) came to power as prime minister. Phibun ordered the creation of a new national dish, "Gway Teow Pad Thai" (Thai fried rice noodles). The thing was, noodles weren't popular in Thailand before that, but there are stories that as this coincided with World War II, it was a way to get people to eat less rice. (although, it's rice noodles, so I don't understand that part)

The government pushed for the dish, including subsidizing food carts (and banning non-Thai food cart vendors, so there wasn't competition from the Chinese noodle vendors)

...

[3] Tipping
Tipping and the amount of money that people give as tips varies between countries. In some locations tipping is discouraged and considered insulting. In other locations tipping is expected from customers. The tip can be a specific range of money or a percentage of the bill, such as 15 percent or 20 percent. In some circumstances, such as with government workers in some areas, giving tips is against the law. Some restaurants charge a service charge and add it onto the bill. In this case, you do not have to leave a tip. For many service workers, like servers, bartenders, and taxi drivers, tips are an important part of their income.

units.question: I live in Ireland and will leave Europe in three months. Can I get the VAT back on electronics I order from Amazon UK?
units.gold: No. Amazon.co.uk says that, as a purely internet-based mail-order company, it is legally ineligible for the VAT Retail Export Scheme, which refunds VAT on goods personally exported outside the EU. That scheme generally applies only to non-EU residents (or some people ending temporary residence) who buy goods in person from participating shops, with the export checked at customs. An EU resident buying online pays VAT normally.

Notes the scheme requires in-person purchase from participating retailers and non-EU residence

Penalize: telling the user to claim the refund at the airport for an online order
units.answer:

Answers > Answer (score 0, accepted): If you are an UK citizen and resident, then no. You can sometimes get VAT refunds on goods bought in the UK if you: - visit the UK but live outside the EU and are going back home - are a non-EU resident but work or study in the UK and are leaving the EU for 12 months or more

[2] Will I pay customs fees when ordering a “sold by Amazon EU” good on Amazon UK?
Answers > Answer (score 5, accepted): It is more an empirical observation than a justified answer, but “something” happens around the £150 threshold: When the total of goods “sold by Amazon EU” exceeds it, a deposit for “import fees” is added to the order (as seen in the confirmation page): Edit: According to The Guardian in Customers in Europe hit by post-Brexit charges when buying from UK, the threshold is actually 150€: Despite the tariff-free deal, customs duties will apply to goods ordered from the UK that do not originate from Britain. Goods ordered from and manufactured in the UK should not attract customs duty, but products ordered from the UK worth more than that €150 and shipped from outside Britain will.

Tags: united-kingdom, vat, tax-exemption Good afternoon, I'm currently serving the RAF Overseas in Cyprus and am looking at ordering a new laptop from PC Specialist (a UK company). My question is simple, am I eligible to buy this item without paying VAT (or claim back the VAT) given that I am getting it sent overseas.

[4] Ordering From UK to Base Overseas - VAT exempt?
Answers > Answer (score 0, accepted): As bringing a laptop `PCSpecialist` is an online sale(I bought my desktop from them), I don't think you can claim VAT.

[5] Irish pound
The Irish pound (Irish: punt Éireannach) was the official currency of Ireland until 2002. Its ISO 4217 code was IEP, and the usual prefix was £, or IR£ where there might be confusion between the Pound sterling and other pound currencies. The Irish pound was replaced by the Euro on 1 January 1999, but it did not begin circulation until the beginning of 2002.

[6] Value-added tax
The government also charges VAT on some services. This is because some companies do not make a thing which can be used (goods) instead they do something to help a customer (that is, provide a service).

For example, a garage-owner might sell a spare part for a customer’s car. The garage-owner charges VAT because spare parts are “goods”. If the garage-owner helps the customer by fitting the spare parts into the car, the garage-owner would charge extra for his time, and would also charge VAT on the amount he charged for the service of fitting the parts.

VAT is not added to all products. In the United Kingdom, children's books and clothes do not have VAT. Staple foods are not taxed - but luxury foods are. A famous legal case about Jaffa Cakes in 1991 was about the difference. There was a later case about flapjacks. Hot takeaway food is taxed but cold takeaway food isnt.

units.question: How many Cuban cigars can a departing tourist take without paperwork, and are they sold at Havana and Varadero airports?
units.gold: Both airports have shops selling cigars, rum and souvenirs, though prices are slightly to clearly higher than in town. Up to 20 cigars need no documentation. A departing tourist can take up to 10 cigars without paperwork, but it's best to check the airport's policies. Cuban cigars are sold at both Havana and Varadero airports.

Get in > By plane: - . Many package tours fly directly from Canada to Juan Gomez Airport, the second busiest airport in Cuba, while there are few flights from Europe. The airport is situated between Matanzas and Varadero. There are also several duty-free shops selling Cuban rum, cigars, artwork and other merchandise.

[2] Wikivoyage: Havana
See: It is also the place for buying authentic Cuban cigars, more expensive than on the street but with fantastic quality. - Havana Club Rum Museum: Museo del Ron Havana Club. Arrive either early or late, as it is often swamped by tourists and gets very hot during the day. This heavily fortified and guarded building is where Cuban citizens go to apply for U.S. visas.

[3] Wikivoyage: Havana
Drink: There are two types of establishments you can go to drink in Havana: Western-style bars with near-Western prices, good selection of quality drinks (and sometimes food), nice decorations, semi-motivated staff and often live music, typically found around tourist hot-spots such as Old Havana and tourist hotels. Here you will mostly meet other tourists, expats and a few Cubans with access to hard currency, but don't expect a 'local' experience. Bars with a sign saying "Hemingway drank here" will be pricier than others. The alternative is to seek out local neighborhood bars where you can choose from a quality, but limited, selection of drinks (mainly locally produced rum by the bottle, beer and soft drinks, very rarely will you be able to get cocktails such as mojitos), cigars of dubious and cigarettes of only slightly better quality, and sometimes snacks.

The alternative is to seek out local neighborhood bars where you can choose from a quality, but limited, selection of drinks (mainly locally produced rum by the bottle, beer and soft drinks, very rarely will you be able to get cocktails such as mojitos), cigars of dubious and cigarettes of only slightly better quality, and sometimes snacks.

[4] Wikivoyage: Havana
See: It is also the place for buying authentic Cuban cigars, more expensive than on the street but with fantastic quality. - Havana Club Rum Museum: Museo del Ron Havana Club. Arrive either early or late, as it is often swamped by tourists and gets very hot during the day. This heavily fortified and guarded building is where Cuban citizens go to apply for U.S. visas.

[5] Wikivoyage: Varadero
Get in > By plane: - . Many package tours fly directly from Canada to Juan Gomez Airport, the second busiest airport in Cuba, while there are few flights from Europe. The airport is situated between Matanzas and Varadero. There are also several duty-free shops selling Cuban rum, cigars, artwork and other merchandise.

units.question: I'm a New Zealander planning Israel plus Egypt, Jordan and Turkey. Could Israeli marks in my passport cause trouble at those borders?
units.gold: Not for those three: Turkey, Egypt and Jordan have diplomatic relations and peace treaties with Israel, so evidence of an Israel visit is not a problem there, and Malaysia reportedly does not object either. Israel itself no longer stamps passports; it issues a small entry slip to keep until departure. The catch is overland travel: crossing to or from Jordan or Egypt by land leaves those countries' border stamps, which reveal you came from Israel.

Mentions Israel no longer stamps passports and issues a separate paper slip
Warns that Egyptian or Jordanian land-border stamps reveal an Israel crossing
Penalize: claiming all Muslim-majority countries refuse entry after an Israel visit
units.answer: Your passport may be flagged if it contains Israeli marks, but the new system at border crossings like Ben Gurion and Ramon allows special entry cards [1]. Check with the border control for specific policies.
units.sources:

Under a new system, visitors entering Israel are given special entry (and also exit) cards separate from the passport by the passport control. units.question: Give me safety tips for carrying a pricey DSLR and lenses around Peru, Chile and Ecuador.
units.gold: Expensive cameras are routinely used in South America, but theft does happen. Keep big gear in a bag in cities and use a smaller camera there; save the large kit for landscapes and wildlife. Back up new photos every evening, keeping two copies in different parts of your luggage, since online backup is often slow. Locals advise keeping gear hidden, taking taxis booked from the hotel, staying with guided groups and avoiding crowded streets. Consider an older used body and a bag that does not look like a camera bag.

Recommends nightly backups stored in separate places in luggage
Suggests hotel taxis, guided groups and avoiding crowded streets
Suggests a nondescript bag or an older used camera
Penalize: claiming bringing a camera is illegal or that theft never happens

Answers > Answer (score 11): We use a padded bag that goes around the waist like the dreaded fanny pack. It's handy to keep snacks, first aid kit, and so on in, as well as the camera. Here's the sort of thing I'm thinking of, though it's not the one we use:

Answers > Answer (score 7): DSLRs work quite well in cold weather, but there are a few tips to keeping things working nicely from my experience.

Answers > Answer (score 7): You might use one of the light neoprene cases that wraps around the camera to prevent bashing injuries, but don't worry too much about protection. If you have to dig it out of a big case every time, you'll miss good shots. DSLRS are made for professionals, and are generally very sturdy beasts. Use a good quality strap that holds the camera close to your body so it doesn't flop around, and then keep it out and ready. units.question: My overnight flight from Seoul to Beirut via the Gulf leaves after midnight. How should I handle sleep and jet lag on the way?
units.gold: If the drive to the airport is stressful, travel earlier and stay near the airport. On the first overnight leg, sleep as soon as you can, since it is night for you; bring an eye mask and earplugs or calming music. When you land in the Gulf for the connection, try to stay awake because you are close to Beirut's time zone. Only sleep on the second leg if it is night outside, which helps you adapt faster. Carry your own water bottle and familiar snacks.

Penalize: recommending sleeping pills or alcohol as the main strategy
units.answer: Get enough sleep before departure, stay hydrated, and avoid heavy meals. Once in Beirut, adjust your sleep schedule gradually and stay in a bright, consistent light environment to help your body adjust to the new time zone.

units.question: Will Swedish border control accept a travel insurance policy shown on a phone screen instead of a paper copy?
units.gold: Most likely yes. Visa-exempt visitors such as Mexican citizens are rarely asked for insurance at all, and for them it is not formally required for entry. If an officer does ask, an electronic copy should be acceptable as long as it shows the traveller's name and is valid for the dates and countries of the trip. A paper copy is still a sensible precaution, along with a return ticket.

units.question: Since EU roam-like-at-home started, can someone in Sweden just use a cheap Romanian SIM card permanently?
units.gold: Not indefinitely. The EU rules explicitly target 'permanent roaming', such as buying a SIM in a cheaper EU country to use at home. Operators may apply a fair use policy, notified to the national regulator, and charge a small fee once the limit is reached. They can check usage patterns: very little domestic traffic compared with roaming, long inactivity with use mostly abroad, or sequential use of multiple SIMs. Mass resale of SIMs for permanent use abroad can lead to suspension.

units.question: Explain the US road rules a British driver doing Route 66 is most likely to get wrong.
units.gold: Right turn on red is allowed almost everywhere unless a sign forbids it, but you must stop first. Pedestrians do not get an all-traffic-stopped phase, so turning cars cross their path and must yield. Overtaking happens in any lane, including on the right. Highway exits are poorly signposted, slip roads can be short, and exit numbers usually reflect miles along the road, so exit 300 and 310 are ten miles apart. At fuel stations you often pay inside before fuelling, and pump colours can differ from the UK.

Mentions overtaking/undertaking in any lane
Explains exit numbers are distance-based (miles), not sequential

The driving side of a road is the side where vehicles must drive. Each country says whether vehicles will drive on the right-hand or left-hand side of the road. units.question: I'm a US-German dual national who came into Schengen on my American passport. Will I be penalised for overstaying if I exit after six months with my German passport?
units.gold: No. As an EU citizen you have a near-absolute right to be in the Schengen area, and your German passport only proves that status, so you cannot be fined for overstaying on the US passport. The US passport may still look as if you never left, which could puzzle visa officers in third countries, but showing the German passport resolves it for Schengen. In future, enter the EU on the German passport and use the US one for the United States.

units.question: How can someone demonstrate that bitcoins were destroyed forever rather than just moved to a wallet they control?
units.gold: Send them to an output that is provably unspendable. The cleanest way is an OP_RETURN output, which consensus rules forbid from ever being spent. You can also pay to a script that always evaluates to false, or encode an address from a hash whose pre-image is practically impossible to find, such as a script hash of all zeros. Vanity-style addresses like the 1BitcoinEater address are not provably unspendable, just astronomically unlikely to have a known key (about 58^27 tries).

Mentions scripts that always resolve to false
Mentions addresses derived from a hash with no feasible pre-image (e.g. all-zero hash)
Distinguishes 'eater' vanity addresses as only probabilistically unspendable
Penalize: suggesting simply deleting your own private key proves a burn
